violations.comments:
2-102.12 (A) PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by being a certified food protection manager. No employee present with active ANSI food protection manager certification. At least 1 employee shall be present during all hours of operation with active ANSI food protection manager certification. REPEAT

For more information on becoming a certified food protection manager please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. Raw chicken stored behind raw beef in top of sandwich cooler. Do not store raw chicken behind raw beef because the raw beef could be contaminated when employees retrieve the raw chicken. CDI - Employee corrected the food storage order. No increase in severity so kept at half credit. REPEAT

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. Nopales in upright cooler measured 45-46F. Employee stated they were cooked this morning at 7AM. CDI - Employee educated on cooling methods and she discarded the nopales. 0 pts.

For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Queso dip measured 115F in hot holding. TCS foods in hot holding shall measure at least 135F. CDI - Employee reheated queso on stove top to above 165F. 0 pts.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf Menudo was cooling on speed rack out of temperature control and measured 95F. Employee stated it was finished cooking 1.5 hours ago. Ensure employees put TCS foods in walk-in cooler or freezer quickly after cooking so the food reaches 70F within 2 hours. Also, nopales were above 41F and cooled in reach-in cooler for over 6 hours. TCS foods must be cooled in proper equipment such as an ice bath, walk-in cooler or freezer. TCS foods must be cooled in shallow pans or containers and left loosely covered or uncovered to facilitate rapid cooling. CDI - Employee educated on cooling methods. Nopales were discarded and the menudo measured below 70F at the 2 hour mark after employee moved pans to the walk-in cooler.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.description: Compliance with variance, specialized process, reduced oxygen packaging criteria or HACCP plan
violations.comments:
8-103.12 Comply with the procedures in the HACCP plan as submitted and approved as part of a variance or local approval. Maintain approval and records as required.-P/Pf
Observed cooling logs void of temperature check at hour 4 for every item tracked in the last month. HACCP plan states cooling items must be checked every two hours. Staff must begin taking cooling temperatures at hour four. Observed employee training log not completed since 2020. HACCP plan states staff who participate in HACCP plan must compete month long hands on training, and verbal knowledge test before signing training log and being allowed to independently partake in HACCP plan. PIC stated multiple employees who actively execute HACCP plan have not undergone this training. Staff training necessary.
10 day VR required.
1 pt.

rows.general_comments:
NOTE: EHS observed temperatures on TPHC log that did not reflect temperatures required on procedures. EHS found reheat temp for chicken 88F written 3 times on 3 different logs. This does not meet requirement for reheating OR TPHC. Temperatures on log should reflect required temps below. If foods do not meet temperature, a corrective action will need to be made. 

Cold holding 41F or below 
Hot holding 135F or above
Reheat commercial cooked foods 135F or above
Raw chicken 165F or above
Ground meats 155F or above
Whole muscle intact meats (steak, pork, lamb, goat) 145F or above

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed multiple items cooling in 2-door RI cooler. EHS observed all items tightly covered with plastic wrap. EHS observed inadequate cooling rates during inspection (see temp chart). EHS observed these items cooling in 2-door RI unit which is actively used throughout service, causing ambient temperature to increase and decrease a lot. Facility has obtained an additional refrigeration to replace drink cooler that was being used in kitchen for raw proteins. EHS suggested dedicating one cooler for cooling and cold holding storage while using the other unit to work out of during service. This way, the “cooling” fridge doors can remain closed so ambient temperature does not fluctuate during the cooling process. EHS advised to removed plastic wrap from items cooling to facilitate more air flow. CDI - PIC removed plastic wrap, and placed all items on ice baths to cool quickly. REPEAT. (1) **This is the third full point deduction for cooling methods. EHS provided education and stated a risk control plan could be implemented in future inspections if improvement has not improved. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. EHS observed raw chicken being stored over raw beef in WIC. CDI - PIC re-arranged storage order, no contamination observed. (0)

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P EHS observed dish machine unable to dispense sanitizer at correct concentration. EHS primed unit and ran a few cycles and observed 0ppm after each cycle. PIC contacted EcoLab and will move to single service items until unit can be repaired. EHS observed food contact surfaces clean to sight and touch during inspection. 3-day VR required. REPEAT. (3)

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed all items in make unit above 41F. PIC stated no items are left in make unit over night. PIC stated items are prepared in the morning and immediately placed into unit for service. PIC stated by doing this, facility was trying to ensure food was fresh each day. PIC stated due to high heat in the kitchen, facility wanted to avoid food being out of temperature. EHS stated that items shall be cooled properly prior to placing into make units for cold holding. Due to high heat and frequency of use items will struggle to cool in make unit. EHS observed ambient temperature of unit at 48F. PIC stated make unit has not been observed in disrepair. Temperatures are checked daily but not documented. PIC stated all food was prepared or removed from WIC at 10:30am. EHS allowed facility to utilize temporary TPHC on items in make unit and instructed PIC to discard items at 2:30pm. EHS provided PIC with TPHC procedure and provided education. PIC stated items will be prepared the night before and placed into WIC over night to cool prior to moving to make unit. EHS emphasized educating food employees on checking temperatures at a frequent rate so that issues observed during this inspection could be prevented. PIC stated facility recently went through some turn over and have had to hire new kitchen staff. EHS stated TPHC is only for temporary use to allow facility to operate, PIC stated make unit will be assessed as soon as possible. 3-day VR required. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

rows.general_comments:
- Facility has changed management since the previous inspection with the PIC stating that it is still under the same LLC, just new managers and staff. Current LLC is still active as of the inspection today. New PIC stated that they are in the process of changing the menu and that despite currently using the old menu they are no longer offering anything cooked to order. Previous management was offering burgers and salmon items cooked to order but current PIC was adamant that they would not offer anything cooked below medium with everything being default to well done. EHS advised staff that the new menus must remove the consumer advisory and asterisks on the burger and salmon items if they would not offer items undercooked.

- For a reinspection, please contact the main office at 980-314-1620.

violations.comments:
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf - Observed multiple priority violations cited out throughout the facility and the PIC to not be know the answers to EHS questions about cold holding temperatures, date marking procedures, or proper dish sanitizing methods. 10 day VR.

A Food Safety Checklist can be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety along with more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.

5-205.11 (A) A handwashing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use Pf. - Observed the handwash sink in the dishwashing area to be obstructed from use by a broom and dustpan placed directly in front of it.

CDI - Broom and dustpan moved.

5-205.11 (B) A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing Pf. - Observed the handwash sink adjacent the soda machine to be used as a dump sink with the basin full of ice upon the EHS arrival.

CDI - Ice melted and education provided on where ice can and cannot be dumped.

6-301.12 Provide paper towels or approved alternative for hand drying at each handsink. -Pf - Observed the handwash sink in the dishwashing area to not have paper towels at the time of the inspection. REPEAT.

CDI - Paper towels provided.

violations.description: Food in good condition, safe & unadulterated
violations.comments:
3-101.11 Food shall be safe for consumption, unadulterated and honestly presented. -P - Observed an insert containers of diced tomatoes and marinara sauce in the 1 door lowboy at the pizza station to be contaminated with mold.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. - Observed an unopened tube of raw ground beef to be stored on the speed rack in the WIC directly above an insert container of raw salmon filets.
- Observed an insert container of raw chicken tenders to be stored directly on top of a box of raw salmon filets in the WIF.

CDI - Storage order rearranged.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P - Observed the chemical dishwasher to be testing at 0ppm sanitizer at the time of the inspection. Dishwasher was found to be hooked up to quaternary ammonia, which is not designed for use in a chemical sanitizing dishwasher. Facility did not have any chlorine sanitizer on site for the chemical dishwasher at the time of the inspection but the machine appeared to be fully functional. 3 compartment sink was also found to not be dispensing properly concentrated solutions. EHS showed staff how to temporarily make a sanitizer solution using the bleach bottle on site and that they must sanitize dishes this way until the dishwasher gets sanitizer or the 3 compartment sink dispenser is fixed. 3 day VR to observe the dishwasher have appropriate chemicals and properly testing for sanitizer. REPEAT.

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. - Observed the deli slicer, a blade to a blender, and multiple stacks of metal insert containers of various sizes to be stored as clean with visible food debris/sticker residue on their food contact surfaces.

CDI - Deli slicer broken down and all dirty items brought to the 3 compartment sink to be W/R/S. EHS advised the facility cover the deli slicer when they are not using it as they stated only using it once every 2 weeks to slice cheese.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed insert containers of raw burger patties, sliced cheddar cheese, cooked diced chicken, and cooked ground beef to be at temperatures of 45-48F in the grill refrigerated drawers. PIC and cookline employee stated that the items remain in the lowboy overnight and are not moved to the WIC at the end of the day. Ambient of the refrigerated drawers was observed at 48F at the time of the inspection. All out of temperature TCS items voluntarily discarded due to being out of temperature for an unknown amount of time. 3 day VR to observe repair to the refrigerated drawers.
- Observed an insert container of buttermilk to be stored on the counter adjacent the fryers at a temperature of 47F. Cookline employee stated they usually store it on ice but the inspection interrupted the set up this morning and they didn’t get to it yet.

CDI - PIC relocated buttermilk to WIC to rapidly cool.

- Observed insert containers of cooked ground beef, cooked diced chicken and portioned bags of cooked penne pasta to be at temperatures of 44-46F in the WIC. All items were not removed from the WIC today and were in the WIC since yesterday as per the PIC and cookline employee.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded all out of temperature items in the WIC.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed insert containers of house made chicken salad, pico de gallo, and chicken wings to have date marks of 6/30, 6/25, and 6/27, respectively. ITS issued for 6th consecutive violation for date marking and the previously implemented risk control plan proving to not be effective for the staff. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded all past date items.

- Observed a container of cheese sauce to be in the WIC and was not provided with a date mark of any kind. Cookline employee stated having made the cheese sauce the previous night.

CDI - PIC date marked cheese sauce.
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

3-304.12 (B) In-use utensils for food that is not TCS must be stored with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed. - Observed scoops in use for the bulk bins of tempura flour and breadcrumbs to be stored with their handles in direct contact with the food inside.

CDI - Scoop handles removed and stored so that the handle does not touch the food inside.

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf EHS observed active cooling during inspection without any managerial control. EHS observed rice cooling without any temperature checks, rice was left at room temperature during entire inspection. EHS advised PIC to move rice to try and meet cooling parameter, however, rice was never moved. EHS cold holding issues in WIC and make units during inspection. PIC unable to provide temperature logs or explain frequency of temperature checks. PIC was not able to answer EHS questions on cooling process and cold holding requirements during inspection. EHS observed no available working thermometers to verify temperatures during inspection. PIC was unable to exhibit active managerial control during inspection for items H & I listed under 2-103.11. EHS will return within 10 days to observe improvement with active managerial control. 

A Food Safety Checklist can be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety along with more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.
6-301.14 Post a handwash sign at each handsink. EHS observed missing hand washing signs by every hand sink in kitchen. CDI - EHS provided PIC with signage. (0)

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. EHS observed a large amount of pans stored clean with visible sticker residue present on exterior of pan. Facility re-uses large plastic tubs for food storage. EHS observed tubs with stickers peeling and present on outside of container. EHS approved tubs can be re-used, however stickers need to be removed prior to stacking for storage. EHS observed immersion blender soiled with food debris. CDI - PIC removed all pans and containers with sticker residue to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. (0)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. EHS observed cooked basmati rice actively cooling on prep counter during inspection. PIC stated rice was cooked at 11:30. By 1:30, EHS observed rice at 89F. EHS observed butter in large cambro sitting under prep table at room temperature. PIC stated butter is unsalted and was melted down yesterday. EHS explained that unsalted butter is TCS, due to melting butter down it would need to follow the same cooling process as mentioned for other TCS items. EHS provided education on cooling methods and parameters and referenced hand outs posted in kitchen. PIC did not exhibit good knowledge on cooling process and was unaware of time parameters that need to be met. CDI - Rice was voluntarily discarded. Due to butter being prepared yesterday, it was voluntarily discarded. (1.5)

For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed numerous TCS items throughout kitchen above 41F. EHS observed WIC at 48F at beginning of inspection. Within 30 minutes WIC cooled to 40F. EHS observed cooked chicken, goat, rice, and paneer in WIC above 41F(See temp chart). These items were prepared yesterday. EHS observed goat, chicken, and curry sauces in make unit above 41F(see temp chart). PIC stated these items were taken from WIC at 11:30 and placed into make unit. EHS observed cooked items in grill low boy above 41F(see temp chart). PIC stated temperatures are checked daily, however, no temp log was provided and EHS observed both food thermometers with dead batteries during inspection. Due to not being able to verify when TCS was last under 41F, TCS food observed over 41F was voluntarily discarded. EHS will conduct 3 day VR to observe long term compliance due to amount of cold holding issues observed and lack of active managerial control during inspection. 

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). EHS observed all items in make units without proper date markings. PIC stated these items are taken from WIC and dates can be verified. EHS explained that this system of date marking is not approved. EHS stated the date product was made shall follow product during all times of preparation/service and shall be discarded after 7 days. EHS verified dates of items in make units with items in WIC. If dates were missing in WIC, both containers were voluntarily discarded. EHS observed milk beverages in drink display cooler in dining room without proper dates. PIC stated beverages are made every Monday. EHS stated that these beverages should be date marked when prepared, even if rotated on a weekly basis. Facility was allowed to date mark milk beverages. EHS will return in 10 days to ensure long term compliance can be achieved and date marking system is in place to monitor dates for products throughout kitchen. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed basmati rice actively cooling on prep counter. PIC stated rice was prepared at 11:30 and is left out for an undetermined amount of time prior to moving to WIC. PIC could not give EHS an exact time food is left out prior to refrigerating after cooking is completed. EHS advised that once cooked fit reaches 135F, the cooling process has began and food must be aggressively cooled within proper time parameters. EHS provided education. CDI - Rice was voluntarily discarded. (0)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

4-302.12 Provide an accessible thermometer for use. Provide a thin probe thermometer for accurate measure of thin foods.-Pf . EHS observed both thin probe thermometers onsite with dead batteries. PIC stated batteries will be ordered ASAP. EHS will return within 10 days to ensure compliance. (0.5)

3-304.12 (F) Containers of water used for storing in-use utensils must be maintained at a temperature of at least 135 F and cleaned at least every 24 hours or when container has accumulated soil or residue. EHS observed in use utensils stored in container of water at 76F. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC removed utensils from water. REPEAT. (1)

violations.description: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled
violations.comments: 4-903.11(B)(1) Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows for air drying. EHS observed numerous pans, stored as clean, stacked on top of each other with water still present on interior surfaces of containers. EHS advised to stagger stack pans to ensure proper air drying prior to stacking. (0)

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. EHS observed non food contact surfaces of equipment throughout kitchen soiled with food residue/debris. This would include interior reach in of make units, gaskets on cold holding equipment, and exterior surfaces of prep equipment. EHS advised to increase cleaning frequency to avoid accumulation. (0)

6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. EHS observed walls around kitchen make line and dish area soiled with food residue and debris. EHS advised to increase cleaning frequency to avoid accumulation. (0)

violations.description: Meets ventilation & lighting requirements; designated areas used
violations.comments: 6-305.11/6-501.110 Designate and use an area for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and possessions. EHS observed employee phone on top of make unit and employee phone and drinks stored dry storage shelving co-mingled with food for service. EHS advised to designate area for orderly storage of employee possessions. (0)

PIC stated temperatures are checked daily, however, no temp log was provided and EHS observed both food thermometers with dead batteries during inspection. Due to not being able to verify when TCS was last under 41F, TCS food observed over 41F was voluntarily discarded. EHS will conduct 3 day VR to observe long term compliance due to amount of cold holding issues observed and lack of active managerial control during inspection.

23 - Proper date marking & disposition: 3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). EHS observed all items in make units without proper date markings. PIC stated these items are taken from WIC and dates can be verified. EHS explained that this system of date marking is not approved. EHS stated the date product was made shall follow product during all times of preparation/service and shall be discarded after 7 days. EHS verified dates of items in make units with items in WIC. If dates were missing in WIC, both containers were voluntarily discarded. EHS observed milk beverages in drink display cooler in dining room without proper dates. PIC stated beverages are made every Monday. EHS stated that these beverages should be date marked when prepared, even if rotated on a weekly basis. Facility was allowed to date mark milk beverages. EHS will return in 10 days to ensure long term compliance can be achieved and date marking system is in place to monitor dates for products throughout kitchen. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction
violations.comments:
3-203.12 Retain tag on the bag of shellstock until empty. Record date on the tag when the last shellstock from the container is used. Store tags in chronological order for 90 days. -Pf
Observed shellstock tag without the recorded date of last sold mussels. Observed shellstock tags not stored in chronological order. EHS observed a metal pan of mussels without a tag present in the lowboy unit on cook line. PIC stated that they were from the large vessel in the walk in cooler, however they only had open tag.
CDI- PIC added the date of 7/3 as that was when they sold the last mussel. PIC stated they were onsite that day and that they received the second bag after finishing the first. PIC placed mussels back in vessel with other mussels from the same bag with the shellstock tag. There was only a singe bag of mussels in the walk in cooler. EHS provided education on the importance of maintaining shellstock tags. 
**10-day VR** EHS will make return visit within 10-days to ensure facility has developed a system for mussels. 
-1-

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. 
Observed multiple dishes with sticker residue present, dishes were stacked so that sticker residue is touching the food contact surface. EHS observed a few dishes with visible food debris.
CDI- Items were taken to dish area to be w/r/s.
**REPEAT** -1.5- 
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

CDI- Cooked lamb was reheated to 165F and placed back on the stove for hot holding as PIC had placed it on the line 30 minutes prior.
*REPEAT* -1.5-

PIC stated that these items are put in the cooler every morning and are stored in the WIC over night. EHS observed ambient temperature of unit at 40F. Items had been in this unit for 4 hours or more, according to PIC. Observed hot dogs and cheeses in cheese RIC with temperatures above 41F. Unit was measuring 35F. EHS gave PIC TPHC procedure sheet to fill out and EHS reviewed procedures for emergency TPHC before end of inspection.

Items had been in this unit for 4 hours or more, according to PIC. Observed hot dogs and cheeses in cheese RIC with temperatures above 41F. Unit was measuring 35F. PIC stated that these items were possibly pulled out of refrigeration to arrange cheeses in containers. PIC unable to verify how long these items were out of temperature. CDI: PIC voluntarily discarded all TCS foods that were above 41F. PIC put in a work order for prep unit and will use emergency TPHC until unit is functioning properly and holding foods at 41F or below. Verification visit required within 3 days to ensure food is in temperature compliance. EHS gave PIC TPHC procedure sheet to fill out and EHS reviewed procedures for emergency TPHC before end of inspection. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

23 - Proper date marking & disposition: 3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) Observed no dates on TCS foods at prep line. PIC stated that they are stocked from a larger dated batch in the WIC. EHS discussed date marking the TCS foods on the prep line to reflect prep date in WIC. CDI: Foods dated to match their larger batch prep dates. Non-dated Items in left prep cooler discarded due to temperature violations.



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

24 - Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records: 3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. Observed house made chipotle ranch, regular ranch held on TPHC near server line and milkshake mix in machine held on TPHC without written procedures. EHS observed that the items were marked with TPHC start times. CDI: EHS provided TPHC procedure sheets for items. PIC filled out procedure sheets and EHS reviewed. 



TPHC procedure template may be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

33 - Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control: 3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf Observed large portion of grilled onions cooling in WIC on a sheet pan that did not meet cooling parameters. PIC and EHS discussed different cooling procedures to ensure onions are cooled quickly. Observed macaroni large deep covered container of macaroni noodles cooling in WIC. Macaroni cooling rate insufficient. CDI: PIC voluntarily discarded grilled onions and moved macaroni to WIF uncovered to continue cooling. violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf
Observed sliced lettuce, shredded cheese, and bottled dressings on TPHC with label incorrectly stating the prep time (when removed from temp control) as the required disposal time. PIC explained that new staff member is still being trained and was experiencing difficulty with the date mark label system. 
CDI- All prep dates verified with GM and prep employee. Items relabeled, correctly, for TPHC. *Disposal should be 4 hours after removal from temp control (if food exceeds 70F), or up to 6 hours if food does not exceed 70F. 

3-501.19(B)(4)(5)Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. The food shall be discarded after the food has completed its 4 hour hold time, if the food is in unmarked containers, or marked with a time that exceeds the 4 hour time limit. -P
Observed bottled ranch, chipotle sauce, mayo, and other TCS dressings at make line labeled for TPHC twice; first label states yesterdays required disposal time, second sticker states today. Assistant manager stated the dressings are cooled in the WIC and put out again with new stickers the next day, which is a TPHC violation. EHS explained that all foods labeled for time must be disposed after 4-6 hours outside temp control. Foods cannot be returned to WIC and placed on TPHC or in cold holding for later use. 
CDI- TCS dressings and sauces voluntarily disposed. (-1.5)

County version of TPHC procedure may be found at: https://mecknc.widen.net/s/pvtc855zds/tphc-template-english
EHS observed McDonalds corporate TPHC procedures onsite. A review with staff is needed to ensure staff understand and execute compliant TPHC.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed approx 7 pans in total of shredded lettuce to be at temperatures of 55-59F in the service line opentop, back service line opentop, and the RIC across from the back service line all of which are units not designed nor approved for rapid cooling. PIC stated that lettuce is washed and cut daily and all items were still actively cooling down. PIC advised to adjust the prep time of the lettuce in the morning to allow for the lettuce to fully cool down prior to opening for service at 10:45am.

violations.comments:
3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. 
EHS observed four pans of chicken in walk in freezer with a temperature of 80F at 3:30pm. PIC stated that the chicken began cooling at 1pm. 
CDI PIC voluntarily discarded the chicken as it did not reach the required 70F in two hours. PIC was knowledgeable about cooling processes such as using ice baths and leaving lids open. PIC provided education to employees. 
-0-
For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed cooked beef, cooked chicken, and cooked tofu and garlic oil holding above 41F in prep unit. Ambient temperature of the unit is 55F. After 30 minutes the units ambient air temperature was 58F. 
CDI- EHS allowed PIC to cool items are they were placed into the unit less than 4 hours from the walk in cooler which is functioning properly. EHS advised facility to utilize smaller prep unit on the line for TCS items until prep unit can be repaired. All items in top of unit are being held on TPHC. 
**REPEAT** 3-day VR Required. 
For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C). Observed the following items on the line without date marks: cooked chicken (x2 in lowboy) cooked beef, garlic oil, seaweed salad, cooked chicken (x2 in walk in cooler) and cooked broccoli. 
CDI- EHS allowed PIC to date items as they were pulled from larger portions in the walk in cooler and PIC was present when items in walk in cooler were prepared. EHS advised PIC that all items should be date marked and not just the larger portions in the walk in coolers.
**REPEAT** -1.5-
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(4)(5)Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. The food shall be discarded after the food has completed its 4 hour hold time, if the food is in unmarked containers, or marked with a time that exceeds the 4 hour time limit. -P 
Observed facility holding nearly all items in top of prep unit on TPHC. EHS observed that after the 4 hour mark employees restarted timers used on the line but did not discard all the items. EHS had to prompt employees and PIC to discard items. Facility must discard all products being held on time after the 4 hour mark. 
CDI- EHS obsevred employees discard all TPHC products.
**REPEAT** -3- 

3-501.19(B) (1) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall have an initial temperature of 41 F when removed from cold holding temperature control or 135 F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. -P
EHS observed cooked chicken being held in prep unit on TPHC. Items had been placed on TPHC less than 20 minutes prior to EHS temping items. Cooked chicken had a temperature of 78F. Chicken had been pulled from container that had not finished cooling in the walk in freezer. 
CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the chicken.

rows.violation_text:
8 - Hands clean & properly washed: 2-301.12 (A),(B) Wash hands for at least 20 seconds. Follow the cleaning procedure to adequately wash your hands. Use warm water, soap, scrub 10 to 15 seconds, rinse, and immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough hand drying method (ex. Disposable Paper Towel). -P Observed PIC drink from her beverage and continue to walk around kitchen handling food and clean dishes without handwashing. Observed PIC wash hands and turn off water with hands then prepare to handle food. EHS intervention, PIC rewashed hands correctly.

For more information on handwashing, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link, https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M .

11 - Food obtained from approved source: 3-201.11(C) Packaged food shall be labeled as specified in Law (e.g. Identify food name, specific ingredients, manufacturer name and address, nutrition information, labeling in English. - Pf Observed canned beverages being offered for sale with no English writing on them. CDI-removed from counter.

15 - Food separated & protected: 3-302.11 (A)(4) Except when the food is being cooled, store food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.
Repeat-Observed various containers of food in WIC with no lid to protect them from possible contamination.
CDI - Lids placed on all containers.

16 - Food-contact surfaces: cleaned & sanitized: 4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. Observed multi use utensils stored in bins as clean sticky/gummy and peelers with dried vegetable between teeth. Multiple pans with peeling non-stick coating, excess seasoning on inside and outside. CDI-items sent back for rewashing.

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P Repeat-Observed sanitizer in 3 comp sink <50 ppm chlorine. CDI-more bleach added and tested a little over 50ppm chlorine. Points no escalated due to improvement


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

23 - Proper date marking & disposition: 3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). Observed most ready to eat items in WIC not date marked. CDI, PIC allowed to date mark items not marked. In the future, the PIC may be required to discard food, per 3-501.18 (A), that is not dated or inappropriately dated in accordance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C). Will do a verification visit for date marking next week.

24 - Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records: 3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf. Observed facility has kimchi on TPHC front area. No time stamps labeling when food was removed from refrigeration. Follow posted procedures. CDI-discussed with PIC that the procedure must be followed or food will need to be disposed of.

35 - Approved thawing methods used: 3-501.13 (A), (B), (C) Use approved thawing methods for frozen food such as in a cooler at 41F or below, completely submerged under cold running water according to the Code, or as a part of the cooking process. Pf. Observed steak thawing on counter. Steak still frozen CDI-put back in cooler/.

44 - Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled: 4-903.11 (A) Store cleaned equipment, utensils, linens in a clean, dry location; where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor. Observed clean utensils stored in dirty bins.

45 - Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used: 4-903.11(C ) Single Service and Single Use items shall be kept in the original protective package or stored using other means that protect the item until used. Observed uncovered toothpicks loose in a container for customers. Toothpicks must be individually wrapped or in a dispenser.

47 - Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used: 4-205.10 Ensure equipment other than toasters, mixers, microwaves, water heaters and hoods is ANSI certified or equivalent. Observed bottled beverage cooler and 2 domestic chest freezers. All equipment should be commercial.

56 - Meets ventilation & lighting requirements; designated areas used: 6-305.11/6-501.110 Designate and use an area for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and possessions.
Observed employee belongings being stored above customer foods during inspection. Ensure all employee belongings are stored in a manner that does not promote contamination of customer foods or service items.
Repeat. 1 pt.

violations.comments: 6-301.12 Provide paper towels or approved alternative for hand drying at each handsink. -Pf observed handwashing sink with broken paper towel dispenser. CDI - PIC added

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed tomatoes, turkey, ham, chicken, pastrami, roast beef, American cheese, provolone cheese, cold holding above 41F in prep top. Ambient is 55F. Observed salami, pepperoni and tuna cold holding above 41F in lower prep unit. Ambient is 43F. Items had been in the unit overnight. All items discarded. EHS checked ambient temp with thermometer along with the foods. PIC stated they do temp checks every morning and food was in proper temperature this morning. EHS observed thermometer broken into pieces in the bottom of prep unit. EHS waited 1 hour to see if unit/TCS foods would cool down. Food temperatures stayed the same. Facility only has one prep top unit to make sandwiches. Facility CAN NOT safely make sandwiches without unit. EHS will arrive back on sight to verify prep unit is cold holding TCS foods 41F and below within 3 days. REPEAT

PIC called the district manager and let them know that unit needs to be fixed or replaced. District manager stated they did not want to voluntarily close. EHS explained that if they do not voluntarily close, the permit will be suspended. EHS explained that if a major piece of equipment is not functioning, it cannot be used. EHS stated they CAN NOT work out of reach in coolers. EHS expressed concern and that it would not be feasible to make sandwiches without a functioning unit. District manager agreed to voluntarily close until unit is repaired 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

Observed pepperoni, salami, and tuna made on a pernicious day without date marking. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P - Observed an insert container of diced cooked steak in the cookline steamtable to be at a temperature of 105-120F. PIC stated that the steak had not been in there longer than 30 mins as they cook small amounts knowing that it is harder to maintain in temperature. 

CDI - PIC rapidly reheated on the stovetop to 165F+.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

PIC stated that the bottles do not stay in there overnight and are brought up to the top before opening at 11am. Bottom portions of bottles and bottles in the lowboy all measured <41F.

CDI - PIC relocated ranch bottles to lowboy and EHS advised that the facility change their holding procedure or switch to smaller bottles.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.comments:
2-301.14 (E) Wash hands after handling soiled equipment or utensils. -P- Observed food employee washing soiled equipment and dishware and then proceed to go and work at the fryer station engaging in food handling with no hand wash in between. -CDI- EHS made PIC aware of observation, PIC went over to the food employee coached him on what occurred, and had him properly wash hands prior to engaging back to food handling. Contamination prevented prior to occurrence. 
Ensure proper handwashing of staff, and ensure that staff is properly trained.

4-702.11 Utensils and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use, after cleaning. -P- Observed a soiled metal pan sitting at the 3-comp sink. Pan was grabbed by a food employee, rinsed with the spray arm, and then about to be used for food prep. Visual soiling was still present on the pan prior to usage. -CDI- EHS informed PIC of observation. PIC stopped food employees from putting food in the container, took the dish to the 3-comp, W/R/S the dishware prior to usage. 
Ensure all food contact surfaces that are soiled are properly W/R/S prior to usage. 





For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P- Observed 2 full large metal containers of chicken in HH adjacent to drive thru, metal containers of chicken were all holding below 135F. EHS asked how long the facility will hold chicken under the light the PIC stated 1-hour prior to discard for quality, and stated chicken should be hot at 140F or above per SOP. -CDI- Chicken was voluntarily discarded by PIC. 
Ensure that food in hot holding is maintained at 135F and above. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments:
4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair. Facility has a non-functioning chicken breading station. Breading station was not being used upon entry into the facility. However, EHS observed facility start to use the station half way through the inspection. EHS discussed with PIC and PIC stated a work order is in for the unit. In the meantime the facility is taking out what they need to be breaded and cooked to the station. Breading all of the chicken quickly in the station and then cooking for HH/Service. Once the batch of chicken breading is completed the batter is removed and brought back to the WIC to cool prior to next use. 
EHS observed no temperature violations in this process during inspection. 
EHS stated to the PIC that it is HIGH PRIORITY to fix chicken breading station. 
EHS is making a follow up visit next week to ensure station is repaired.

violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf- Observed sliced tomatoes, cut lettuce, and tuna cooling in WIC in deep metal pans, covered tightly with plastic lids and stacked on top of each other. -CDI- PIC immediately unstacked cooling containers and removed lids for rapid cooling. CDI - PIC brought spoons to the dishwasher to be W/R/S and will keep avocado spoons in water in the tabletop steamtable going forward.

violations.comments:
REPEAT.
3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P 
Observed grilled chicken breast and plantains below 135F in hot box.

rows.general_comments:
Facility utilizes spirulina powder. Additive is approved. 
REHS and PIC are determining whether or not collagen powder derived from bovines is approved. Facility is not currently using collagen, but would like to resume its use.
Facility is receiving energy bites from The Naked Tart and bottled juices from Green Brothers Dilworth location. Prior to the next inspection, foods shall either be prepared in the establishment or obtained from an alternate approved source.

violations.comments:
4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P- Observed sanitizer in the 3-Comp sink being dispensed at 0PPM. PIC and EHS attempted adjusted the 3-comp sanitizer dispenser, however dispenser was still reading at 0PPM. PIC and EHS read the manufacturers instructions to achieve proper food contact sanitize concentrations. PIC established that 1.5 Oz of sanitizer in 5.5 gallons of water was the ratio to achieve 300 PPM for manual chemical mixing. EHS and PIC tested the sanitize solution and it was 300PPM. 
Facility has called a service request for the chemical tree and will manually mix sanitizer using concentrations and test prior to usage until repaired. 
EHS will make a return visit tomorrow to ensure fixed.

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf Observed no employee health forms in facility. Each employee needs to review the procedures and plans and to sign and date the forms, which shall be accessible at all times. Only found form for one employee.
Will need to return within 10 days to find that forms are available and signed and dated, for all employees.



A Food Safety Checklist can be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety along with more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P 
Observed white rice at 119F - 124F. Must cook and hold hot foods to at least 135F. Took white rice and re-heated to greater than 165F, and returned item to hot holding on prep line. 


For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed bags of cooked chicken in walk-in cooler that were divided into bags yesterday with no dates marked on them. These must be marked with the date if they are going to be held for more than 24 hours. CDI by marking dates on bags. 


For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed shredded cheese in several bins to be tightly covered and at 43F. These need to be loosely covered so that air can cool food more quickly. CDI by loosening food wrap so that air can cool food. 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

4-502.11(B) Provide accurately calibrated thermometers. Pf. 
Observed 2 of the 3 thin probe thermometers to not be working properly. Either have these repaired or discard them so that staff do not try to use them to check food temperatures. 

For information on how to properly calibrate a thermometer please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following weblink: https://youtu.be/IxXix712KkI
4-204.112 (B) Provide and position correctly an air thermometer in cold/hot holding equipment. Observed that no thermometer could be found in Coke refrigerator that was holding milk products. Obtain a properly calibrated thermometer and place it in this refrigerator. Need to return to see that this thermometer has been obtained and placed into this refrigerator.

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta. Observed spice in container with no product name on container.

2-303.11 Remove jewelry on hands and arms while preparing food. A plain ring, such as a wedding band, is allowed. Observed several employees wearing watch, bracelet, and ring with stones. No watches or bracelets are allowed to be worn by food service employees, and only smooth rings with no stones are allowed to be worn.

violations.description: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled
violations.comments: 4-901.11(A) After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall not be used until air dried or adequately drained before contact with food. Observed some pans stacked wet - these must not be stacked until they are completely air-dried.

violations.description: Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used
violations.comments:
4-903.11(A)(C) Store single-use and single-service articles in a clean, dry location; where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor. Boxes of single service utensils stored on floor. These must be stored so that they are at least 6 inches above the floor surface.

4-904.11 (A) Display and handle single-use and single-service articles and cleaned and sanitized utensils to prevent contamination. Observed single service cups stored outside of a dispenser and outside of the original plastic wrap that they are shipped in. Either store these in the original plastic bag, or have a properly calibrated thermometer dispenser that will protect the cups from handling the mouth-contact surface and will also protect the cups from sneezes, coughs, dust, etc.

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments: 4-501.12 Resurface or replace cutting surfaces that can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized. Observed several cutting boards that were very scarred and not easily cleanable. These either need to be re-surfaced so that they are smooth and cleanable, or replaced with cutting boards that are in good repair. (d) Food and beverage equipment and supplies shall be located in enclosed areas and protected from environmental contamination when not in operation. Observed long cutting board for front prep area was standing on one end on the floor, and was then picked up from floor and placed onto counter to use. No food contact surfaces are allowed to be placed onto floor.

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed black counters up front with exposed particle board surfaces due to damaged laminate. These areas need to be repaired and shelves need to be of non-absorbant materials such as marine hardwood, stainless steel, etc.

violations.description: Management, food & conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities & reporting
violations.comments:
2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure.-PF- *Observed - No proof of training for staff regarding foodborne illnesses and symptoms. *CDI - EHS provided copy of employee health policy and reporting agreement for PIC to have current and future staff read, sign and date.

For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

*REPEAT* 3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D).

4-602.11 (E )Clean the equipment and utensils used with nonTCS foods as required to avoid contamination. EHS observed minor black residue accumulating along the sides of interior surfaces of ice machine. EHS advised to increase cleaning frequency to avoid accumulation. (0)

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. EHS observed lobster sauce cooling in WIC above 70F (see temp chart). PIC stated sauce was started at 9:30a and finished cooking at 10:00a. PIC stated neither cooking or cooling temperatures were documented. Based on the last known time when food was removed to be prepared, EHS advised sauce has not properly cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F. 3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed cooked onions, raw seabass, raw hamburger beef, steak, and crab cakes above 41F during inspection (see temp chart). violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed lobster sauce prepared in house which failed to meet cooling parameters. EHS observed sauce left open in WIC, but observed thin film over sauce. PIC stated sauce was prepared by morning employee and left in WIC. EHS advised to continuously stir and monitor temperatures to ensure compliance with cooling parameters and methods. EHS observed raw shrimp cooling in WIC from being thawed and portioned, PIC stated this item was just portioned 30 min prior to inspection. EHS observed shrimp portioned in plastic bags and stored in WIC to cool. EHS observed double stacked pan of portioned shrimp with ice pan on bottom. EHS observed temperature of shrimp in contact with ice bath under 41F. However, EHS observed temperature of container not in contact with ice only decreasing 3 degrees in 30 minutes. EHS advised to spread out portioned shrimp onto sheet pans or place all in ice bath to quickly cool. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded lobster sauce due to missing cooling parameters, PIC spread shrimp out onto ice bath to ensure adequate cooling. (0.5)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.description: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
violations.comments:
3-403.11 (A),(D) Reheat all TCS foods to 165F within 2 hours if food is to be hot held until service. -P - Observed 2 container of rice to be slowly reheating in the tabletop steamtables at a rate of .833 degrees/min, which would result in the rice to not reach 165F within the required 2 hour reheating timeframe. Rice was observed at 66F after 30 mins of reheating. PIC stated this is a new process of reheating the rice as they’re trying to retain moisture after receiving complaints from customers that the rice is “crunchy”. EHS advised that the staff rapidly reheats on the stovetop before transferring to the steamtable.

CDI - Rice removed from steamtable and rapidly reheated on the stovetop to 165F+.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed an insert container of raw chicken to be at a temperature of 44F in the bottom refrigerated drawer at the cookline. All other items in the drawer were observed at 41F or lower. 3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P EHS observed chicken burritos in hot box under 135F (see temp chart). PIC showed EHS temperature log. violations.description: Management, food & conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities & reporting
violations.comments:
2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure.-PF - Observed the facility to have signed employee health agreements on site but the agreements on site only had 5 reportable illnesses and not the required 6. Non-typhoidal salmonella was observed to be missing from the current signed forms.

CID - EHS provided updated copies of employee health policies with all 6 reportable illnesses.

For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P - Observed an insert container of raw clams to be stored on the top shelf of the lowboy refrigerator across from the stovetop, directly above containers of cooked vegetables. REPEAT.

CDI - Storage order rearranged, clams moved to the bottom shelf.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed containers of rosemary butter, miso butter, and scampi butter to be stored on the prep table adjacent the steamtable at temperatures of 70-76F. PIC stated that all butter mixtures are made from unsalted butter.

CDI - PIC placed items on temporary TPHC and time stamped the items for discard. EHS held conversations with the PIC on switching to salted butter or permanently holding the items on TPHC going forward to remain in compliance. New TPHC form would be required to be filled out if they opt to go with that method.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed an insert container of cooked vegetables to be stored in the cookline lowboy across from the stovetop and was not provided with a date mark of any kind. PIC stated that the vegetables were from the night before.

CDI - PIC date marked item.

- Observed an insert container of cut sausage to be stored in the cookline lowboy across from the stovetop with a date mark of 7/10, making today day 11. PIC stated it was for a pasta dish that he is no longer serving.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.comments:
6-301.14 Post a handwash sign at each handsink.
Observed a missing hand wash sign for the main kitchen hand sink.

3-DAY VERIFICATION REQUIRED
3-201.11(A) Use food from approved sources only. -P 
Observed vacuum sealed chicken salad, egg and tuna salad. Employees stated that these come from Cheney Brothers but were unable to provide invoices during inspection. EHS has emailed owner to request invoices. Establishment will not use the ROP products until invoices are provided.

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. 
Observed raw chicken stored on top of sausage in the walk-in cooler. CDI - Items were moved to the correct order.

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed one bag of cut lettuce with no date mark. CDI - Items was labeled for the day it was prepared.

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta.
Observed one large bin of sugar without a label. Observed missing labels for oil squeeze bottles.

REPEAT
2-402.11 Use head coverings, beard guards and clothing to restrain body hair from contacting exposed food, equipment, and utensils.
Observed two employees preparing food without hair restraints.

violations.comments: 5-205.11 (B) A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing -Pf- Observed sponges, debris, and deli cup present in rear hand sink upon the EHS arrival. Ensure that hand sinks are used for hand washing only. -CDI- Items removed from hand sink.

4-602.11 (E )Clean the equipment and utensils used with nonTCS foods as required to avoid contamination. Observed the inner portion of the ice machine with debris and residue present. Ensure that ice machine is cleaned, maintained as clean, and cleaning frequency is increased. 

4-703.11 After cleaning, equipment, food contact surfaces, and utensils shall be sanitized using an approved method.-P- Observed food employee at the 3-comp sink washing and rinsing soiled equipment. EHS did not observe a sanitize step occurring. When EHS asked why the 3rd basin was not filled with sanitizer the PIC stated that the food contact surfaces are sanitized with a spray bottle of chlorine bleach and immediately rinsed. EHS notes that chlorine concentration was above 200PPM. EHS also notes that the contact time on the sanitizer manufacturers label states that dishes must soak for 2 minutes. -CDI- EHS coached food employee and PIC on proper sanitizing at the 3-Comp sink. PIC filled the sanitize basin with water and added chlorine bleach (liquid) per the manufacturers instructions for sanitizing food contact surfaces. After this was done the chlorine levels were reading at 100PPM. EHS told the PIC to write down this procedure and to train staff and check levels often enough to make sure that they are correct. Dishes were then placed back into the W/R/S process. 
Ensure proper W/R/S process is maintained and continued

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P- Observed a spray bottle of bleach being used to sanitize dish ware at the 3-Comp sink. Sanitizer bottle was over 200PPM. -CDI- spray bottle was diluted and EHS coached PIC on proper sanitizing practices at 3-comp (see comment above). 






For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. violations.comments:

No contamination observed of these foods during inspection. 
Ensure that food is kept off the floor.

Observed hot water dish machine unable to reach 160°F. Max ambient is 153F. PIC stated they have gotten a new dish machine it has been unable to reach temperature for several days. PIC stated they reached out to company, but has not had a chance to follow up. PIC stated they have not been sanitizing dishes. Establishment shall only use single use items such as disposable plates, cups, and utensils until dish machine is repaired and working properly. violations.comments:

violations.comments:
3-304.15(A) Discard gloves after a task is complete or any time they are damaged or soiled. -P- Observed food employee handling a soiled dry rag and then going back to food preparation without a glove change or hand wash in between. Ensure that food employees are changing gloves and washing hands after gloves are soiled. 
-CDI- PIC spoke with food employees and educated them on proper glove usage. Food employees then washed hands and performed a proper glove change.

4-602.11 (E )Clean the equipment and utensils used with nonTCS foods as required to avoid contamination. Observed buildup of the residue and debris present in the inner portion of the ice machine. Ensure that ice machine is cleaned and cleaning process is increased. 


4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf- Observed cutting blade of the can opener soiled with debris present. PIC stated that the facility does not use this can opener and instead uses a hand held can opener. EHS explained that even if this is not used, it is still a food contact surface and must be maintained as clean even in storage. -CDI- PIC moved can opener to 3-comp sink for W/R/S. 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P- Observed home fries at 124F on expo lamp HH. EHS asked PIC how long they had been in HH to which PIC stated 20 mins. EHS provided PIC with options to reheat to 165F or above or to discard. 
-CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded potatoes. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P- Observed the majority of food in prep top 1 unit above 41F. EHS asked the PIC if the food was held over night to which the PIC stated that it was. Ambient temperature of the unit was 46F. -CDI- Food was voluntarily discarded. PIC determined that the unit has an air flow issue and that the unit needed to be adjusted to achieve better air flow. PIC also turned the temperature of the unit down. Facility is monitoring the unit and called a technician to the facility to service the unit. EHS provided the facility with a TPHC sheet to perform emergency TPHC procedures. EHS will make a return visit tomorrow to ensure that the unit is functioning properly. 
Observed egg mix above 41F in PT 2 as well as melons. -CDI- Food was voluntarily discarded. All other TCS food in the unit were 41F or below. 
Observed lettuce in a container in LB 2 above 41F. -CDI- Lettuce was voluntarily discarded. 

Ensure that facility improves cold holding for long term compliance. EHS recommends daily log keeping of cold holding temperatures. Further non-compliance in cold holding may lead to a risk control plan. 
TPHC SHEET EMAILED
3-DAY VR. 
EHS will make a return visit to assess cold holding. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .
