violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. Observed no written procedures for TPHC. CDI- PIC had a blank copies of the template and filled out during inspection. 
3-501.19(B)(4)(5)Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. The food shall be discarded after the food has completed its 4 hour hold time, if the food is in unmarked containers, or marked with a time that exceeds the 4 hour time limit. -P Observed food being removed from TPHC after 3.5 hours and placed in the tall reach in coolers for cold holding. CDI- All items on TPHC were discarded. EHS explained to manager that once an item in on TPHC it cannot be reverted back to temperature control. Items must be discarded only. 
3-501.19(B) (1) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall have an initial temperature of 41 F when removed from cold holding temperature control or 135 F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. -P Observed foie gras and garlic confit placed on TPHC prior to being cooled to 41F. CDI- Items cooled to 41F in blast chiller.

violations.description: Compliance with variance, specialized process, reduced oxygen packaging criteria or HACCP plan
violations.comments:
3-502.11 Obtain a variance for specialized processes.-Pf Observed eggs cured in salt, dehydrated at 90F overnight in dehydrator unit. After dehydration, egg yolks are removed from dehydrator and place in the refrigerator for holding. Eggs are then held for 3 days. CDI- Discarded. Eggs cannot be dehydrated at 90F overnight without a variance. Eggs can be cured in salt in the coolers holding at or below 41F and held for no longer than 7 days (this was the previous process discussed with managers and EHS).

For more information on how to apply for a variance please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. 3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed four (4) portions of TCS food (raw chicken, raw shrimp, and raw beef in prep top, raw chicken in prep unit) above 41F. PIC stated that the items were prepared day of inspection, but that prep top had been opened to during lunch. -CDI- PIC placed chicken in the WIF to be quickly cooled to 41F. Prep top lid was closed to correctively cool TCS foods in prep top portion. EHS observed items at 41F or below by the end of the inspection.


For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). Observed approximately nine (9) items in server RIC (salad bin and salad bowls) with door date marks denoting date of prep of 7/13. Per conversation with PIC, date marks were placed on Monday (7/13), but had not been changed to reflect salad portions prepped on day of inspection (7/15). CDI - Door labels were changed to reflect date of preparation.

Note: as described, establishment uses containers with date labels to hold TCS food portions (trays with individual salads, bins holding rice bowls, etc.) and cross out original dates once portions are complete to add new label. EHS advises removal of old labels and writing new label, so as to denote that a new portion of TCS food is being stored. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

Note: No escalation in point deduction due to some noted improvement from previous inspection; fewer portions of thawing ROP fish were observed having not been removed from deoxygenated environment.

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf -Observed cooked tempura shrimp held on 4-hour TPHC with no label identifying the time which the food was removed from temperature control. -CDI - PIC verified when shrimp tempera was originally removed from temperature control (11am) and properly added time stamp.
-REPEAT-

3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. -Observed no written TPHC procedures for fried rice held on 4-hour TPHC. EHS observed proper time stamp on fried rice. -CDI- PIC added fried rice to 4-hour TPHC procedures.



TPHC procedure template may be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
-Observed steamed broccoli miss cooling parameters after cooling too slowly overnight. Observed broccoli at 45F, stored in deep pan and covered with lid. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the broccoli. 
-Observed spicy tuna cooling in low reach-in cooler, after being prepped this morning. Low reach-in coolers are not efficient at cooling. Use small portions, uncovered shallow containers, within the WIC or freezer for efficient cooling. -CDI- Spicy tuna was still within its 4-hour cooling window, so PIC moved tuna to freezer for rapid cooling.


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.comments:
4-703.11 After cleaning, equipment, food contact surfaces, and utensils shall be sanitized using an approved method. -P-
Observed dish machine not reach 160F despite several cycles. Machine is also able to do chemical sanitizing. violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P Observed approximately eight (8) portioned bags of mozzarella in counter display cooler used to hold TPHC salads above 41F. Observed right side prep unit at ambient temperature of approximately 52F (no TCS food stored within at time of observation.) Observed left side prep unit ambient temperature at 58F, with all TCS foods (approximately nine (9) portions of sliced meats, sliced mozzarella, cooked shrimp, etc.) at between 48F and 52F. Per conversation with PIC, doors of units had been open during breakdown of units (removal of TPHC products.) PIC voluntarily disposed of mozzarella portions and rotated all TCS foods in right prep unit to WIC to cool correctively. A verification of cold holding equipment will occur no later than 7/16.

Note: EHS observed portioned mozzarella cheese in grab n go cooler actively cooling from prep and cooler with an ambient temperature of 38F. EHS will assess cooler for its ability to cool and cold hold TCS food upon verification visit. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments: 3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf Observed approximately seven (7) bags of portioned in house grated cheese blend (Asiago, Parmesan, and Romano) at counter top with no labeling. Per observation of the cheese original packaging, portions are to be held under refrigeration. Per conversation with PIC, cheeses are portioned daily and voluntarily disposed of prior to the end of each shift. CDI - EHS and PIC reviewed TPHC procedures held in house; procedures were amended to include bagged portions of cheese to be held at either room temperature for 4 hours or less or at 70F or less for up to 6 hours, starting from their removal from the WIC.

EHS observed corrective handwashing performed by employee at newly restocked hand sink and effective handwashing throughout inspection.

4-602.12 (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure. Observed minor soils accumulation inside of microwave. Per conversation with PIC and observation, microwave is used to thaw wrapped and sealed raw animal foods, which are then fully cooked via stove top. Clean interior as needed.

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Observed one (1) rice cooker of brown rice at temperatures between 127F and 133F. Per conversation with PIC, rice had been prepared on morning of inspection less than 30 minutes prior to EHS arrival. CDI - Food employee removed rice from pot and reheated to above 165F via wok at stove top. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). EHS observed proper use of date marking and labeling via white board and direct labeling in cold holding units (I.E. prep unit underside and WIC.) However, EHS observed one (1) TCS food item (sweet and sour chicken pieces) on whiteboard labeled as frozen on 6/29 and marked on bag as 6/24, while thawing in WIC at 38F. Per conversation with PIC, item had been improperly marked on bag based on white board, and thaw date had not been written on bag or board. CDI - EHS demonstrated thawing procedure by writing thaw date of 7/12 on whiteboard. Refine system used to track prep and thaw dates of TCS foods. REPEAT.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - 0 pts - Observed sour cream and ricotta cheese based sauces reading 54-65F. PIC will explore if changing the location of storage will assist in maintaining temperature or explore if TPHC is needed.

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). / 3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed the date marking system for items in the flip top units not sufficient to ensure all products have proper labeling. Items such has mushrooms, tomatoes, ham, lettuce, onions, steak, chicken, and other items were not properly dated. Currently the establishment does not label product on the top of all flip top units due to the items being stored directly under in the reach ins with dates. During the inspection most products in the flip tops did not have a direct item under the unit that indicated the date. The establishment must create a system to ensure date follows product throughout the entire process. CDI - During the inspection PIC labeled all products based on prep logs. Establishment will label products on units moving forward. 

Verification Required - EHS will return to evaluate the new system in place for items stored on the prep line. 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
violations.comments:
3-403.11 (B),(D) TCS food reheated in a microwave shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of 165 F within 2 hours and the food is rotated or stirred, covered, and allowed to stand covered for 2 minutes after reheating if food is to be hot held until service. -P
Observed queso that was reheated in microwave and only reached 146F. CDI placed back in unit for more time and reached 189F.

3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. 
Observed facility with 4 pans of pico that was prepped this morning and only reached 50F past 4 hours. CDI items discarded. Observed large bin of shredded lettuce in reach in prep unit that was cooling and only reached 53F. CDI items discarded discarded.

REPEAT.
4-101.19/4-202.16 Non FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent
cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.
Observed unsealed wooden shelves in dry storage area which are heavily deteriorated, no longer smooth and cleanable. Replace or resurface shelving at earliest opportunity. (-1)

violations.description: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained & used; test strips
violations.comments:
4-501.14 Warewashing machines and the compartments/drainboards of sinks used for washing and rinsing equipment, utensils, raw food, etc. shall be cleaned before use, throughout the day to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils, and at least every 24 hours if used.
Observed severe accumulation of dark residue on loading/drainage racks for dishes to be placed into chemical dish machine. EHS advises they clean and sanitize racks today. 

4-501.18 Maintain wash, rinse, and sanitize solutions clean.
Observed severely soiled water in use at wash basin of 3 comp sink.
CDI- Basin drained, sanitized, refilled. PIC advised to ensure basin are maintained clean and water is changed when the bottom of basin is no longer clearly visible. (-0.5)

REPEAtT.
6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure.
Observed black buildup, food splatter, and general need for cleaning to walls, attachments, and behind equipment throughout kitchen. Increase cleaning frequency. (-0.5)

rows.violation_text:
15 - Food separated & protected: REPEAT.
3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P 
Observed uncovered container of raw shrimp behind raw peppers and cooked sausage in top cook line cold drawer.
CDI- No contamination observed. Raw and RTE swap places, RTE foods lidded. (-3)

22 - Proper cold holding temperatures: 3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed salsa’s between 45-55F at expo prep top ice bath. EHS confirmed they were placed their this afternoon form WIC. 
CDI- Salsas rapidly cooled in WIC and placed on TPHC. EHS discussed TPHC with PIC at length. (-0)

STEPS: 
1. Fill out procedures and retain copy onsite. 
English version- https://mecknc.widen.net/s/pvtc855zds/tphc-template-english
Spanish version- https://mecknc.widen.net/s/jb7hdwsqqk/tphc-template-spanish
2. Ensure food begins at 41F or below.
3. Label items with discard time- 4 hours from removal of temp control.
4. At end of 4 hours, PIC must ensure discard. Do not cool and re-use remaining.

violations.comments:
3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. Observed raw chicken stored over pork/beef in WIC. Facility has menu item that is portioned into bags with three different raw proteins. EHS advised that proteins should be stored according to highest cook temperature. Therefore, the portioned proteins would need to be stored on the bottom shelf. CDI - PIC moved portioned proteins to bottom shelf. No contamination observed. 
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P EHS observed raw fish being stored over RTE foods in make unit reach in compartment. CDI - PIC re-arranged storage order. No contamination was observed. 
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation (1.5)

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. EHS observed sticker residue present on exterior surfaces of numerous pans; stored clean. EHS observed pans stacked on top of each other in storage. PIC stated facility wants to switch to different labeling stickers but did not know if that was allowed. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC instructed food employee to remove pans with sticker residue to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. 
For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .


4-602.11 (E )Clean the equipment and utensils used with nonTCS foods as required to avoid contamination. EHS observed ice machine soiled with black/orange residue around door to ice machine EHS observed ice machine door in disrepair and creating areas that are hard to clean. PIC stated ice machine is in the process of being removed. Facility has additional ice machine in good condition. EHS observed both ice machine full of ice and in use during inspection. CDI -PIC stated ice machine will cleaned out and not used until removed. (0)

violations.comments:
3-302.11(A)(8) Separate unwashed produce from ready-to-eat foods. Observed unwashed produce stored over washed produce in the WIC. Ensure washed produce is stored above unwashed produce to prevent possible contamination.


For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation
3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P Observed raw shell eggs stored over packaged ready to eat foods (i.e.-radishes, smoked sausage) in the WIC. Ensure raw foods are stored below ready to eat foods to prevent possible contamination. CDI- PIC voluntarily moved raw eggs to bottom shelf. REPEAT.



For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. Observed two meat cleavers and a knife stored as clean on the wall magnet holder with food residue still on them. CDI- PIC removed the meat cleavers and knife to the warewashing area. REPEAT


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .
4-602.12 (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure
The interior of the microwave had food debris build-up and needs to be cleaned frequently. CDI- PIC had it cleaned during inspection.

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P. Observed a bowl of raw beef stored in fliptop unit #2 holding at 45F. CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the raw beef. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 

Also observed cooked food items in the 2 door cooler at wok station held past 7 day expiration. The food items were- eight bags of cooked pork (6-17), one bag of cooked beef (6-22). CDI-PIC voluntarily discarded the pork and beef in the 2 door cooler. REPEAT.



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .
3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 

Observed several bags of cooked pork dumplings in the standing 2 door RIF. These bags need to be date marked with the prep date. REPEAT. A verification will occur within 10 days.



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments: 3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf. Observed cut cabbage, egg noodles and rice noodles not marked on the white board with a time per TPHC procedure. CDI- PIC filled out times for the items during inspection.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf Observed a plastic bin containing cooked chicken that was cooling at a rate of .43/min which is below the required rate of .54. Ensure proper cooling methods are used. REPEAT. A verification will occur within 10 days.



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.comments:
3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P- Observed shredded lettuce that was prepared at 5:21 AM this morning per the sticker present on the lettuce. EHS took a temperature of the lettuce at 9:26 AM and the lettuce was 43F-44F. Lettuce was cooling in a lowboy in a tightly wrapped container. Ensure that ambient prepared foods cool to 41F within 4 hours. -CDI- lettuce was voluntarily discarded. 





For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf- Observed ambient prepared lettuce miss the cooling window. The lettuce was cooling in a wrapped plastic container in the lowboy. Ensure that the facility uses proper cooling methods such as venting containers and using larger equipment such as their WIC to cool. -CDI- Lettuce that missed the window was voluntarily discarded.

rows.general_comments:
Arrived at facility, PIC stated they were having issues with the WIC which was not properly holding ambient or TCS items 41F and below. PIC stated that they had a temporary cold holding trailer with a lock delivered and in use since Saturday. PIC stated due to limited space in cold holding trailer, staff was utilizing WIC to cool items utilizing ice baths. During inspection observed some TCS items cooling in ice baths. Observed multiple TCS items (cut tomatoes, shredded cheese, cut lettuce), prepared earlier today (7:30 am), holding above 41F. All items throughout facility that were holding 41F and above were voluntarily discarded. 
Facility manager voluntarily closed facility and will not open until WIC has been successfully repaired.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed a large bus bin of lo mein noodles to be cooling at a rate of .083 degrees/min and to miss the first cooling window with the noodles at 76F at the 2 hour mark. Bin was observed to be deeply filled, densely packed with noodles, and had plastic wrap covering the top of the container which all do not allow for adequate cold air flow around the product to facilitate proper cooling. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded due to it not reaching 70F within the first 2 hours of cooling.

- Observed approx 10-12 containers of smoked crab and a tray of kani to be observed at temperatures of 44-47F in the sushi counter lowboy refrigerator. As per the sushi employee all items were prepared that morning and immediately placed into the sushi lowboys to be used throughout the day. Date marks on the containers supported this statement. Containers of smoked crab were observed with tight fitting lids on and the tray of kani was observed with tight plastic wrap over the top of it, not allowing for adequate cold air flow around the product to facilitate proper cooling. Lowboy refrigerators are also not designed nor approved for rapid cooling and all cooling must be done in the WIC. REPEAT.
- Observed a container of cooked beef to be at a temperature of 94F in the cookline lowboy refrigerator and was observed to be actively cooling down per the cookline employee. Employee stated having cooked the item within the last hour before placing it in the lowboy, which is not designed nor approved for rapid cooling.
- Observed a container of lo mein noodles to be at a temperature of 66F in the cookline lowboy refrigerator and was observed to be actively cooling down per the cookline employee. Lo mein noodles were from the same bulk batch that was observed actively cooling in the WIC. Employees stated they needed noodles up at the cookline so they had taken from the batch still cooling and placed them in the cookline lowboy to use during lunch, which is not designed nor approved for rapid cooling.

CDI - PIC moved all items to the WIC to rapidly cool. Lids and plastic wrap removed from items.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-302.12 Label all working containers of food (oils, spices, salts, flour, sugar) except food that is easy to identify such as dry pasta. - Observed all secondary containers used on the wok line rolling cart for spices, seasonings, and sauces to not be labeled as to their contents.
- Observed the bulk bins of sugar, flour, MSG, and rice in the dry storage area to not be labeled as to their contents.

CDI - Door closed.

violations.description: Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used
violations.comments:
4-903.11(A)(C) Store single-use and single-service articles in a clean, dry location; where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor. - Observed multiple stacks of plastic to go containers and lids at the cookline to be stored with their food contact surfaces face up, allowing for the potential contamination of the food contact surfaces.

4-502.13 Single-use and single-service articles cannot be reused. - Observed plastic single service containers to be in use as bulk bin scoops throughout the facility.

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments:
4-501.12 Resurface or replace cutting surfaces that can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized. - Observed a cutting board to have large chunks missing, heavy scarring, and heavy staining which rendered it no longer easily cleanable.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded.

violations.description: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained & used; test strips
violations.comments:
4-501.18 Maintain wash, rinse, and sanitize solutions clean. - Observed the wash basin of the 3 compartment sink to be filled and active warewashing to be going on at the time of the inspection and the wash water was observed to be heavily contaminated with food debris/grime. All dishes go through the chemical dishwasher after being hand scrapped/washed.

CDI - PIC changed solution and EHS discussed with staff the proper times to change the wash water.

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. - Observed the racks used in the dishwasher to have heavy accumulations of black grime. REPEAT.

violations.description: Meets ventilation & lighting requirements; designated areas used
violations.comments:
6-305.11/6-501.110 Designate and use an area for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and possessions. - Observed a bin containing employee food and ingredients for employee meals such as raw pork to be stored on the middle shelf of the WIC, directly above boxes of raw vegetables to be used for consumers. REPEAT.

CDI - PIC relocated employee bin to lower shelf of the WIC.

Use suitable utensils, single-use gloves or dispensing equipment. -P - Observed the PIC touch lo mein noodles with their barehands to check the temperature of the product while it was cooling down.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded all contaminated lo mein noodles.

- Observed a container of raw shrimp to be stored on a shelf in the WIC directly above the large bus bin of lo mein noodles that were actively cooling. REPEAT.
- Observed a container of raw shrimp to be stored on the top shelf of the cookline lowboy refrigerator directly above opened packages of fries and dumplings containing precooked pork and chicken.

CDI - Storage order rearranged in the WIC, on the WIC speed rack, and in the cookline lowboy so that all RTE items are stored above all raw products.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

CDI - PIC changed sanitizer bucket. After priming and a couple cycles the dishwasher was observed dispensing a proper 150ppm chlorine solution.

CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded bus bin of lo mein noodles.

21 - Proper hot holding temperatures: 3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P - Observed a fryer basket full of sesame chicken to be at temperatures of 101-110F at the time of the inspection. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded basket of chicken.

Back of establishment needs to be cleaned and all items need to be put in trash can for avoid access to insects.

Increase cleaning frequency and thoroughness of floors walls and ceilings.

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed cardboard lining shelves with Pepsi bottles. Remove cardboard and use a washable liner if needed. REPEAT VIOLATION Previous violation corrected.

violations.description: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
violations.comments:
5-501.113(B) Keep dumpster, outside waste containers covered with tight-fitting lids or doors. Observed opened doors on the dumpsters. 
5-501.115 Discard items and litter stored in the waste areas and enclosures as they are not necessary to operation and maintenance. Observed excessive amounts of bulky items in the dumpster enclosure including pallets, equipment, and umbrella. PIC informed engineer who will schedule a bulk pickup to remove the items.

rows.violation_text:
2 - Certified Food Protection Manager: 2-102.12 (A) PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by being a certified food protection manager. Observed no CFPM present at time of inspection. REPEAT VIOLATION

For more information on becoming a certified food protection manager please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

3 - Management, food & conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities & reporting: 2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure.-PF Observed no signed/confirmation of employee health policy training on site. PIC was able to answer questions regarding information about the employee health policy but indicated they do not have a policy she has signed. CDI: Policy signed during inspection today. 




For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

24 - Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records: 3-501.19 (A) (1) Written procedures for Time as a Public Health Control shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the establishment, and made available for the Health Department upon request. Written TPHC procedures must specify methods of compliance with 3-501.19 (B) or (C). -Pf. Observed no written procedures for items held on TPHC. CDI: Procedures filled out during inspection. 



TPHC procedure template may be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

37 - Food properly labeled: original container: 3-602.11(C) Bulk food available for consumer self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled in plain view with the manufacturer label provided with the food, or another method of identification that includes the information in 3-602.11 (B)(1), (2), and (6). Observed no common name or ingredients information as required for self dispensed cereals. CDI: Common names provided. Facility still needs to meet the rest of the rule. 
3-602.11 (B) (1)-(4)Food packaged on premises for customer self service shall include a label with the (1) common name of the food; (2) ingredients and sub ingredients in descending order; (3) quantity of contents; (4) name and place of business. Observed individually wrapped bagels and english muffins with no labeling. CDI: Bagels and English muffins unwrapped. 
3-602.11 (B) (5) Food packaged on premises for customer self service shall include a label with the major food allergens contained in the food -Pf. Observed individually wrapped bagels and english muffins with no labeling. CDI: Bagels unwrapped.

39 - Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display: 3-306.11 Protect food on display using shields, packaging, or other effective means. -P Observed unprotected food items including grit/oatmeal toppings, cheese and salsa, and grits. VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 3 days on or before 7/4 to ensure food is adequately protected. Facility may use physical monitoring, self closing containers or other physical barriers such as sneeze guards.

45 - Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used: 4-903.11(C ) Single Service and Single Use items shall be kept in the original protective package or stored using other means that protect the item until used. Observed overstacked cups and cups without protection for coffee, milk, and water.

47 - Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used: 4-205.10 Ensure equipment other than toasters, mixers, microwaves, water heaters and hoods is ANSI certified or equivalent. Observed air fryer in back kitchen labeled “household use only”. Remove equipment. REPEAT VIOLATION Previous violation corrected. 
4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair. Observed gasket on right door of reach in cooler torn.

48 - Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained & used; test strips: 4-302.14 Provide a test kit that accurately measures sanitizer concentrations. -Pf Observed quat sanitizer test strips and expired since 2022 and physically damaged. Test strips were not accurately testing sanitizer. VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 10 days on or before 7/10 to confirm test strips are on site.

49 - Non-food contact surfaces clean: 4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed cardboard lining shelves with Pepsi bottles. Remove cardboard and use a washable liner if needed. REPEAT VIOLATION Previous violation corrected.

54 - Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained: 5-501.113(B) Keep dumpster, outside waste containers covered with tight-fitting lids or doors. Observed opened doors on the dumpsters. 
5-501.115 Discard items and litter stored in the waste areas and enclosures as they are not necessary to operation and maintenance. Observed excessive amounts of bulky items in the dumpster enclosure including pallets, equipment, and umbrella. PIC informed engineer who will schedule a bulk pickup to remove the items.

violations.comments: 5-205.11 (A) A handwashing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use Pf. Observed hand sink to right of cook line and hand sink behind sushi prep line with no running water. PIC stated a pipe was leaking from near cook line which required service technician to shut off water temporarily. CDI: Running water to both hand sinks was restored during inspection.

3-302.11(A)(8) Separate unwashed produce from ready-to-eat foods. For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation Observed a box of unwashed mangos being stored on shelf in reach in cooler in bakery area over ready to eat foods and boxes of unwashed produce being stored on a shelf in walk in cooler above ready to eat foods. CDI: PIC re-arranged items to proper storage order.

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ . Observed two containers of mashed potatoes being held below 135F in hot box. CDI: PIC reheated mashed potatoes to over 165F before returning to hot hold.

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs . Observed containers of cooked mushrooms, cooked rice and cooked noodles being stored in prep cooler on cook line with date marks ranging from 6/15 to 6/17, several days past their expiration. CDI: PIC discarded expired items. REPEAT.

3-501.13 (E ) Reduced oxygen packaged fish, required to be kept frozen until time of use per labeling, shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing under refrigeration or upon completion of thawing using running water. Observed a package of amberjack fish fully thawed in walk in cooler still in its reduced oxygen packaging. Package stated remove from packaging prior to thawing. CDI: PIC cut open package to remove from reduced oxygen environment.

3-304.12 (B) In-use utensils for food that is not TCS must be stored with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed. Observed a scoop being stored handle down in a large container of sugar. CDI: PIC removed scoop from container of sugar.

violations.description: Consumer advisory provided for raw/ undercooked foods
violations.comments:
3-603.11 (A) Provide consumer advisory for animal foods served raw or under-cooked. Consumer advisory must include disclosure and reminder.-Pf. 
Observed deli portion of establishment without consumer advisory for new cold smoked salmon offered on menu. VERIFICATION REQUIRED on or before 7/10 to assess establishment consumer advisory. 

3-603.11 (B)(2) Consumer Advisory Disclosures that are asterisked to a footnote shall state, * Items are served raw or undercooked, or contain (or may contain) raw or undercooked ingredients. -Pf. SEE COMMENT ABOVE.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf. Observed TCS foods throughout establishment cooling in active units, covered containers, and in ice baths missing stirring step. CDI- EHS discussed ensuring units are maintained closed when not in use, items are cooled in units not being actively used, items are cooled in containers that are shallow and are maintained without lidding, use of ice bags as necessary. All items were removed to rapidly cool using larger cold holding units and ice bags. *REPEAT*



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.comments:

cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. violations.comments: 5-205.11 (B) A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing Pf. EHS observed hand sink by make line full of ice during inspection. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC removed ice from hand sink. REPEAT. (1)

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P EHS observed dish machine unable to dispense chemicals at proper concentration during inspection. PIC stated unit has only been used a few times this morning. PIC instructed food employee to prime unit and run another full cycle prior to checking. CDI - EHS observed proper concentration after unit was primed and a full cycle was ran. (0)

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed all items in WIC above 41F during inspection. During initial assessment, EHS observed WIC at 43F, WIC quickly cooled to 41F within minutes. PIC stated food employee checked temperatures at 10:30am and everything was under 41F. PIC unable to locate today’s temperature logs. PIC stated the first employee that arrives to the kitchen is required to do a temperature check. Facility has installed data loggers in WIC to keep track of ambient temperatures. PIC showed EHS temperature line graph showing the last 24 hours of ambient temperature. EHS observed WIC has been above 41F for the last 24 hours. PIC stated due to temperature issues and information available from the data loggers, all TCS foods not prepared today will be voluntarily discarded. By the end of inspection, EHS observed WIC at 38F. EHS advised to complete temperature logs daily to ensure food temperatures are being documented. EHS did not observe any active cooling in WIC during inspection. EHS observed one item cooling in make unit during inspection. PIC stated items are placed into WIF to cool. All items in WIF at 41F or below. PIC voluntarily discarded all TCS foods in WIC that have been in unit overnight or longer than 4 hours. Repair technician arrived onsite as well to ensure unit is functioning as it should. Repair technician stated everything on unit is working properly. Repair technician stated that evaporator on unit is going bad but is still able to operate; part has already been ordered and will be installed within two days. EHS will conduct 3-day VR to observe long term compliance with cold holding. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed cut cabbage, cooked noodles, and raw eggs above 41F during inspection. EHS observed two containers of cut cabbage in WIC 2 (WIC closest to door) above 41F. This is the only TCS item facility stores in unit. EHS observed ambient temperature of unit at 42-43F. This unit never cooled below 41F during inspection. EHS observed cooked noodles and raw eggs in WIC 1 (middle WIC) above 41F. EHS observed ambient temperature at beginning of inspection at 44F, by end of inspection middle WIC was observed at 40F. Majority of TCS foods in middle WIC observed right at 41F during inspection. PIC removed items cooling into WIF to finish cooling within time parameters. EHS observed ambient temperature of kitchen at 96F. PIC unable to verify if temperatures were taken today. PIC will contact repair technician to have both WIC assessed to ensure units can hold TCS foods at 41F during service. EHS will return in 3-days to assess units and compliance with cold holding. This unit never cooled below 41F during inspection. EHS observed cooked noodles and raw eggs in WIC 1 (middle WIC) above 41F. EHS observed ambient temperature at beginning of inspection at 44F, by end of inspection middle WIC was observed at 40F. Majority of TCS foods in middle WIC observed right at 41F during inspection. violations.description: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
violations.comments: 3-403.11 (A),(D) Reheat all TCS foods to 165F within 2 hours if food is to be hot held until service. -P Observed meatballs reheating in steam table. PIC stated they start them in the microwave but that the target is at least 140F but not over 160F. The container of meatballs was being reheated for the second time and therefore must hit 165F. After 40 minutes, the meatballs had risen approximately 30 degrees and still had approximately 30 degrees left to go with 20 minutes left. CDI: Item continued to be reheated in the microwave to over 165F in the microwave. Meatballs going up to commercial reheat were also placed in the microwave due to them tracking to not make it to the required temperature as well. EHS recommended stirring throughout reheating processes. See temp chart.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
4-301.11 Provide equipment in number and capacity so that cooling, heating, and holding temperatures are achieved. -Pf
Observed WIC over capacity during inspection. Excess storage of foods blocked condenser fan, prohibiting it from being able to circulate cold air properly, leading to improper cold holding temperatures. Ambient air on bottom two shelves against the back wall and under the condenser observed maintaining 43/44F, despite the condenser pushing out air at 40F. Facility has one small WIC, two 2 door RIFs, one 1 door RIC, and three prep units. REHS observed at least 14 items that are cooled from hot in facility/on the menu. PIC stated they receive two deliveries per week. REHS advised PIC to increase deliveries to three times per week, utilize RIFs for cooling, and to rearrange WIC to allow for better air flow and to prioritize TCS foods being held in areas of WIC that maintain proper temperatures.
10 day VR required.
0.5 pts.

20 - Proper cooling time & temperatures: 3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. Observed tomatoes in walk in cooler prepared at 4:30am still above 41F. CDI: Tomatoes voluntarily discarded. EHS provided suggestions to PIC regarding cooling including but not limited to adding ice to the water after using veggie wash so the tomatoes remain 41F and below during preparation. Then, be sure to slice and place tomatoes in the walk in immediately after prep. EHS also discussed different placement of the tomatoes as they were right next to do the door. Record date on the tag when the last shellstock from the container is used. Store tags in chronological order for 90 days. -Pf. Observed only one shellfish tag for oysters in the last 90 days. PIC indicated that other tags were accidentally discarded. CDI- by educating PIC on proper shellfish tag retention requirements.

20 - Proper cooling time & temperatures: 3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. Observed carrots, potatoes, zucchini, plantains and cabbage cooling on counter upon arrival. All items were cooked at approximately 10:15-10:30am. PIC placed items over ice on counter. Ice bath was insufficient to properly cool foods in required time parameters. CDI- items placed in shallow pans in walk in cooler to ensure parameters were met. Repeat violation. If violations occur at next inspection a risk control plan will be required to be implemented. 



For more information please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

21 - Proper hot holding temperatures: 3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Observed all foods in steam table below 135F. Steam table was not on due to breaker tripped. CDI- steam table turned back on and all foods reheated to above 165F. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

23 - Proper date marking & disposition: 3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) Observed dates on several items not being carried through to working containers on line. Pico, queso and cooked onion carrot mix were labeled with today’s date in prep units but products were prepared yesterday. CDI- items allowed to be redated with yesterday’s date. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

33 - Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control: 3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf Observed cooked carrots, zucchini, cabbage and potatoes cooling on counter in kitchen upon arrival with no active method for cooling. Air temperature in kitchen was above 85F. Ambient air cooling will not meet cooling parameters. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.comments:
3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. -Observed raw katsu chicken stored above raw shrimp in the reach-in freezer. Raw katzu chicken was previously thawed and prepared at facility (breaded). -CDI- PIC corrected storage order. -No point escalation due to significant improvement in storage order noted in storage order since last inspection. All storage order in prep coolers and WIC was correct. -1/2 points-


For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
-Observed prepped cream cheese in low reach-in cooler above 41F. All other foods in cooler were properly cold holding at or below 41F. Date mark showed cream cheese was prepped two days ago, and PIC stated cream cheese has not been removed from cooler since preparation date. -CDI- PIC lowered ambient temperature of cooler and EHS observed temperature of cooler drop to 36F. PIC voluntarily discarded the cream cheese.
-Observed steamed broccoli above 41F in wok prep top, stored in container directly on top of other foods. Broccoli was steamed this morning and needed for lunch service use. All other foods in the cooler were properly cold holding at or below 41F. -CDI- PIC moved steamed broccoli to WIC for rapid cooling. By end of inspection, EHS observed broccoli cooling at sufficient rate to reach 41F within 6 hours of steaming. EHS recommended steaming broccoli a day in advance, so that the broccoli has sufficient time to cool in the WIC and be moved to the wok prep unit for use the next day.


For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments: 3-501.19(B)(3) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Food shall be marked to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control. Pf -Observed one container of kani held on 4-hour TPHC without a time stamp stating when the kani was removed from temperature control. All other foods held on 4-hour TPHC had a correct time stamp (rice, other containers of kani, eel). EHS also observed proper TPHC procedures for all foods held on 4-hour TPHC. -Significant improvement in TPHC procedures and implementation noted since last inspection. No point escalation- 1/2 points-

3-501.13 (E ) Reduced oxygen packaged fish, required to be kept frozen until time of use per labeling, shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing under refrigeration or upon completion of thawing using running water. -Observed ROP tuna thawed in prep cooler, still within the ROP bag environment. -CDI- PIC cut hole in bag to remove it from the ROP environment.

violations.description: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display
violations.comments: 3-305.14 Unpackaged food shall be protected from contamination during preparation. -Observed bottom of food container directly touching the top of crab meat in prep unit. Crab meat container did not have lid to protect the food from contamination. -CDI- PIC placed lid on crab meat container.

3-304.12 (A) In-use utensils in TCS food, must be stored with handles above the food and top of the food container.
Observed tongs used to dispense cooked noodles stored with the handle in contact with the food. -CDI - PIC removed the handle from the food. 
-REPEAT-

violations.description: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled
violations.comments: 4-903.11 (B) After cleaning and sanitizing, clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying and covered or inverted. -Observed wet stacking among multiple dishes, stacked and stored as clean. -CDI- PIC separated the containers for proper air drying.

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments:
4-101.19/4-202.16 Non FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent 
cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.
-Observed cardboard with visible food residue stored on top of seasoning bowls. PIC stated cardboard is used to protect the seasoning bowls from contamination. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the cardboard. Going forward, PIC stated employees will use plastic wrap to cover and protect the seasonings from contamination.

violations.comments:
7-201.11 Store toxic materials to avoid contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service/use items. -P - Observed a bottle of floor cleaner to be stored on a sry storage shelf amongst opened packages of spices and seasonings.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf - Observed approx 30-40 packages of various grab & go sushi rolls to be at temperatures of 43-47F in the sushi display case, sushi 2 door lowboy, and sushi sliding door lowboy. All rolls were prepared today at approx 8am. Sushi employee stated that there is less room in the shared WICs on Mondays so they use the other refrigerators to cool the prepped sushi rolls down. Lowboys, grab & go cases, and sliding door lowboys are all not designed nor approved for rapid cooling.

CDI - All actively cooling sushi rolls moved to the WIC, where they were then observed at 40F by 10:15am.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

CDI - Scoop removed so handle is not in contact with the mocha powder.

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. - Observed the interior/exterior gasket area of the cheese lowboy and the sliding door tracks of the deli display case to have accumulations of food debris/grime. REPEAT.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf Observed cooked mushrooms cooling at ambient room temperature on sheet tray. Cooked mushrooms had a temperature of 74F and had been removed from oven 1 hour prior. CDI - Cooked mushrooms were moved to walk in cooler to rapidly cool to 41F or less. -0 points-

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.13 (A), (B), (C) Use approved thawing methods for frozen food such as in a cooler at 41F or below, completely submerged under cold running water according to the Code, or as a part of the cooking process. Pf Observed frozen packages of beef thawing at ambient room temperature on prep table. CDI - Packages were taken to walk in cooler to continue thawing under refrigeration.
3-501.13 (E ) Reduced oxygen packaged fish, required to be kept frozen until time of use per labeling, shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing under refrigeration or upon completion of thawing using running water. Observed thawed ROP Salmon in refrigerated drawer that had not been removed from oxygen free environment. PIC has been advised to follow thawing instructions printed on each individual package. -0.5 points-

violations.description: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display
violations.comments: 3-305.11 Store food in a clean, dry location, not exposed to contamination. Keep at least 6 inches above the floor. Observed packages of chicken breading mixture stored on platform less than 6 inches above the floor. Raise as needed.

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed grease and flour residue build-up on the sides of the fryers; observed sticker residue on the outside of cleaned food containers that were stored above the 3 comp sink; observed the WIC floor and shelves with residue build-up and needing cleaned. Increase cleaning frequency to prevent build-up. REPEAT. 

Note: no escalation in point deduction due to some improvement; drink machines, WIC surfaces, and prep areas were observed as clean at time of inspection.

violations.description: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
violations.comments: 5-501.113(B) Keep dumpster, outside waste containers covered with tight-fitting lids or doors. Observed top lids missing on recycle dumpster unit. Replace lids.

6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. Observed the floor area under and around the fryers has residue and debris build-up and needs to be cleaned. Ensure frequent cleaning to prevent build-up. REPEAT.

Note: No escalation in point deduction due to some improvement; previously cited ceiling tiles and WIC flooring have improved based on previous observations and entries.

violations.comments:
3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P EHS observed raw tuna stored over RTE sauces in sushi reach in unit. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC rearranged storage order. (0)

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P EHS observed dish machine unable to dispense sanitizer during inspection. Facility has used dish machine since opening. PIC assessed unit and stated tubing installed on unit to deliver sanitizer has holes present and prevents the liquid from reaching unit. CDI - PIC was able to repair unit during inspection. EHS observed unit dispensing chemical at correct concentration prior to end of inspection. (0)

For more information please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg and How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P EHS observed numerous TCS items in WIC and 2-door sushi LB above 41F(see temp chart). After thirty minutes EHS observed no change in temperature. PIC stated on Wednesday ice build up was observed on back of unit in WIC. PIC stated units thermostat was adjusted to help with the freezing and must have been turned up too much. PIC stated yesterday WIC was observed at 42-43F, in response PIC turned unit back down. PIC was unaware the 2-door LB was in disrepair. PIC voluntarily discarded all TCS foods in WIC and 2-door LB and contacted repair technician. Due to additional refrigeration space and limited number of TCS items needed for service, facility will be allowed to temporarily operate while unit is being repaired. Facility will not be allowed to cook/cool any items until unit is repaired and must only store non-TCS foods inside WIC during this time, all other TCS foods shall be stored in extra units in kitchen area. All TCS items in sushi 2-door LB and WIC were voluntarily discarded. Sushi station has additional 2-door LB that is mainly used and all items can be sufficiently stored inside. EHS will return on Monday to ensure repairs have been done. If WIC has not been repaired, and IS will be issued. (1.5) *** Prior to EHS leaving facility EHS observed WIC at 40F, EHS advised facility to continue with what was previously discussed. Facility was advised to monitor internal temperature throughout the evening to ensure unit can consistently maintain temperature below 41F prior to beginning to utilize unit again. PIC stated repair tech will arrive at 6:30 to assess 2-door LB sushi unit and WIC. 

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

PIC stated that items were thawed/cut this morning and verified with items in reach in unit. EHS stated during last inspection, all items in sushi display shall be dated marked. PIC discussed issue with sushi chef who verified dates with prep list from this morning. CDI - PIC was allowed to date all sushi items. PIC stated moving forward all items will be dated. violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments: 3-501.19(B)(4)(5)Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. The food shall be discarded after the food has completed its 4 hour hold time, if the food is in unmarked containers, or marked with a time that exceeds the 4 hour time limit. -P EHS observed toss salad mix being stored at expo window on time. EHS observed TPHC sticker past 4 hour hold. EHS notified PIC. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded salad mix. (0)

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed cooked mushrooms, onions, tomatoes cooling from being prepared 30-45 minutes prior to inspection according to PIC. EHS observed items cooling at room temperature. EHS observed temperatures above 70F. PIC stated food is left out at room temperature until food has begun cooling and then placed into WIC. EHS advised that item only has two hours from time cooling begins to be under 70F. PIC removed items from speed rack and placed into WIC with tight fitting lids. EHS observed inadequate cooling rates after thirty minutes. At this time, these items had a remaining 20 minutes to achieve proper cooling. EHS intervened and advised to stretch items on sheet pans and placed into WIC to quickly drop temperature to meet parameters. CDI - PIC stretched onions, mushrooms, and tomatoes onto sheet pans and placed into WIC. EHS verified prior to two hour window and observed temperatures below 70F. (1) REPEAT. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) EHS observed today’s date on all items in both make units. PIC stated they mark items for the day it was placed into unit, not the day it was made. PIC stated they can verify the date it was made to ensure it is not held beyond 7 days. PIC stated in previous inspections, facility was told this was within code. EHS provided education. Facility will date mark all ingredients in make units with the day the product was made moving forward. EHS allowed PIC to verify all items in reach coolers and provide accurate dates for all items in make unit. EHS observed small trays prepared to accompany soup entrees. These small trays contain various TCS items to be used with the soup. EHS observed the same date marking process with the trays as seen with the make units. PIC stated trays are dated for the day they were prepared. EHS provided education stating that unless each item is dated individually, or items are discarded daily, the oldest date shall be reflected and used as the correct date mark for the trays to ensure compliance with date marking. PIC adjusted date to reflect this. EHS will return in 3 days to observe compliance. If incorrect dates are observed on items during VR, items will be required to be discarded. (1.5)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

1. Ensure food starts at 41F or below.

3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P.

Observed sliced spinach, lettuce, couscous, chorizo, feta cheese, diced tomato, and mayo in cold well/lowboy above 41F. See temp chart. 
CDI- Items rapidly cooled in WIC. EHS advises that lowboy was overfilled past its capacity, and cold air cannot circulate if fans are blocked. Ambient air in unit observed at 40F. *Risk Control Plan or permit action may be taken if cold holding is out of compliance at the next inspection, due to repeat violations.

CDI: PIC removed date label and created new date label with correct prep date.

CDI: PIC voluntarily discarded potatoes.
Observed pan of crab cakes date-marked with prep date of 6/18, stored inside make table 2. PIC stated this is a food item they freeze then thaw, and stated they thawed this item on Tuesday (6/23).
CDI: PIC created second date label to depict the "clock start" date.
Observed pan of tomato cream date-marked with prep date of 6/16, stored inside the WIC. PIC stated this was not correct and was actually prepared on Friday (6/19).

violations.comments:
4-703.11(B) After being cleaned in a mechanical dish machine, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in the dish machine by achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by a max/min thermometer.-P. 
After checking dish machine final rinse gauge and running department disk thermometer through the machine, it was discovered that disk thermometer showed 148F on final rinse, and in-place thermometer on machine showed final rinse of 139-140F. Person running dish machine needs to know what to look for when processing utensils. Facility also needs to purchase a disk thermometer in order to monitor maximum temperature of final rinse to be at least 160F. Facility has called company so that they can repair the dish machine. Utensils must be processed through 3-compartment sink to properly wash, rinse, and sanitize. VR visit must be made within 3 days to see that dish machine is properly running and properly sanitizing. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following weblink: Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed par-cooked chicken wings at 46F in refrigerator; conversation with kitchen manager as well as observation of other food items in this refrigerator shows the appearance that these wings were likely left out on a counter before being placed in refrigerator. Chicken wings come from reach-in freezer where they are at 32F, and all other items in the refrigerator where the chicken wings were at 46 were at 39F. Assure that items are removed from bag and that bag is then placed quickly back into refrigerator. CDI by items being placed on sheet tray into walk-in freezer, where they were later measured at 31F.


For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Consumer advisory provided for raw/ undercooked foods
violations.comments:
3-603.11 (A) Provide consumer advisory for animal foods served raw or under-cooked. Consumer advisory must include disclosure and reminder.-Pf
3-603.11 (C )(2) A Consumer Advisory Reminder shall include asterisking the food item to a footnote that states: * Consuming raw or undercooked meats, poultry, seafood, shellfish, or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness.- Pf
Observed no consumer advisory present on facility's online menu. Facility's physical menu has consumer advisory.
Observed no asterisks on any menu items for facility's physical menu correlating with the footnote. PIC stated caesar dressing is made in-house and includes raw eggs. PIC also stated steak is cooked to temp per order. The following menu items will need asterisks included to be in compliance for facility's consumer advisory: Surf & Turf, Caesar Salad, Side Caesar Salad, Chicken Caesar Wrap, Huevos Rancheros (on brunch column) any option to have caesar dressing as the dressing or sauce for menu item, any option to sub chicken for steak on bowls, and any option to add steak as a protein for salads. 
VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 10 days to ensure facility is in compliance.

violations.comments:
7-102.11 Label working containers of toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers.-Pf
Observed one unlabeled spray bottle stored at the dish area. PIC stated that the liquid inside the spray bottle was degreaser.
CDI: PIC labeled spray bottle as degreaser for easy identification.

Observed food employee actively engaging in food prep with bracelets on.
Ensure food employees remove all jewelry from hands when engaging in food prep to prevent contamination.

violations.description: Consumer advisory provided for raw/ undercooked foods
violations.comments:
10-DAY VERIFICATION REUQUIRED
3-603.11 (A) Provide consumer advisory for animal foods served raw or under-cooked. Consumer advisory must include disclosure and reminder. -Pf
3-603.11 (C )(2) A Consumer Advisory Reminder shall include asterisking the food item to a footnote that states: *Consuming raw or undercooked meats, poultry, seafood, shellfish, or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness. -Pf
Observed missing disclosure, consumer advisory and asterisk for ceviche on the bar menu. Observed missing advisory on the menu board and paper menu. 

The correct, full statement should read: 
*This item is served using raw or undercooked ingredients. Consuming raw or undercooked meats, poultry, seafood, shellfish, or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness.” Asterisks should be placed before the statement and before ceviche on the menu.

REPEAT
2-303.11 Remove jewelry on hands and arms while preparing food. A plain ring, such as a wedding band, is allowed.
Observed one employee preparing chips and salsa while wearing an ornate ring.

3-304.12 (F) Containers of water used for storing in-use utensils must be maintained at a temperature of at least 135 F and cleaned at least every 24 hours or when container has accumulated soil or residue.
Observed a utensil for cleaning out salsa containers inside of 70 degree water. EHS recommends storing utensil in an empty cup and washed, rinsed, sanitized every 4 hours.

6-501.11 Floors, walls, and ceilings including the attachments such as soap and towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vents shall be maintained in good repair.
Observed increased paint chipping on the floor throughout the kitchen.
