violations.comments:
4-703.11(B) After being cleaned in a mechanical dish machine, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in the dish machine by achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by a max/min thermometer.-P. 
Observed high temp dish machine unable to reach 160F after multiple cycles were run. PIC stated last time ECOLAB was on-site for routine maintenance was early this month. PIC contacted ECOLAB rep for repairs. ECOLAB rep stated they will make a visit tomorrow morning. Facility has properly concentrated QUAT sanitizer used at the 3-compartment sink. PIC stated they will only utilize the 3-compartment sink to wash/rinse/sanitize all multi-use equipment and utensils until repairs have been made.
VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 3 days to ensure facility is in compliance.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following weblink: Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

violations.description: Consumer advisory provided for raw/ undercooked foods
violations.comments:
3-603.11 (C )(2) A Consumer Advisory Reminder shall include asterisking the food item to a footnote that states: * Consuming raw or undercooked meats, poultry, seafood, shellfish, or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness.- Pf
Observed no asterisks for consumer advisory on new menu, which includes 5 menu items that are served raw or undercooked. Under "shareable plates" section, spicy tuna crispy rice (for raw tuna chunks). Under "signature entrees" section, Korean power bowl (for sunny side egg). Under "Brunch" section, 1) avocado toast 2) breakfast smashburger 3) fried chicken biscuit sandwich (all for undercooked eggs).
VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 10 days to ensure facility is in compliance.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed two pans of sliced tomatoes cooling at a rate of 0.05 deg/min, inside the blast chiller, unable to meet the cooling rate. Tomatoes were cooling inside the blast chiller in plastic plans that were tightly covered with seran wrap. Date labels showed tomatoes had been just prepared and placed inside to cool.
CDI: PIC removed seran wrap to allow proper cold air flow.
Observed cast iron dishes of portioned out spinach dip cooling at a rate of 0.09 deg/min, inside the drawers of make table 1, unable to meet the cooling rate. Cast iron dishes were covered with seran wrap. Spinach dip was prepared less than 4 hours prior to EHS's observation. 
CDI: PIC removed seran wrap from spinach dip and moved dishes into the blast chiller to rapidly cool down.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

NOTE: EHS spoke with PIC about air conditioning issue. Air conditioning has not been working at the facility. All units have been affected due to the lack of A/C. EHS inspected Maroon market 6/24/26. During inspection EHS found that the prep top was not functioning as stated my the PIC at Maroon Market. The ambient air temp was 65F. Facility currently has very limited volume and is able to serve out of the cold drawers for now. EHS will verify that the unit is fixed within 3 days. Kitchen area was very hot during inspection. If facilities are not able to safely serve food due to increased temperatures, facilities will have to close. EHS asked to speak with owner of the operation, however PIC did not have a contact.

EHS spoke with several vendors at Monarch market about the air conditioning issue. Several vendors have had issues with keeping up with food temperatures since the air conditioning stopped working. Food safety needs to be maintained at all times. If food safety cannot be maintained, push for compliance will follow. 





For questions please contact EHS at 980.402.4689

violations.comments:
4-703.11(B) After being cleaned in a mechanical dish machine, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in the dish machine by achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by a max/min thermometer.-P. Observed high temperature dish machine not reaching 160F for sanitizing according to EHS plate thermometer. PIC called maintenance to address the issue and EHS observed technician arrive on site during inspection. CDI: Dish machine now reaching 160F for sanitizing. 


For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following weblink: Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-401.11 Cook raw animal foods to required temperatures. Do not interrupt the cooking process without approved procedures. -P Observed sliced roast beef in RIC drawer at sandwich prep line. PIC stated that the roast beef is cooked on a spit at wood fired oven to 110F, sliced, cooled, cold held, then cooked to 165F for service per order. PIC does not have approved procedures for non-continuous cooking in facility. PIC stated that they will fill out an application for procedures to continue this procedure once approved. PIC stated that until procedures are approved, roast will be cooked to 130F for 110 minutes to be in compliance with the food code. CDI: non-continuous cooked roast beef voluntarily discarded.

3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. Observed large plastic bin with lid holding raw whole chickens in a cold brine solution in WIC cooling from yesterday.chickens were measuring 43F-45F. CDI: PIC added ice to brine solution to quickly cool raw chickens to 41F or below. EHS observed chickens at 38F by end of inspection. PIC stated that room temperature water is put into the brine solution and placed in the WIC to cool. PIC stated that they are now going to start adding ice to the solution to ensure chickens are cooled quicker. 




For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf Observed raw whole chickens in large, tightly covered plastic bings in a cold brine solution that was cooling over night with temperatures above 41F. CDI: PIC added ice to bins to quickly cool chickens to below 41F and will use ice for their procedure going forward to ensure chickens are cooled quickly. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

3-501.13 (A), (B), (C) Use approved thawing methods for frozen food such as in a cooler at 41F or below, completely submerged under cold running water according to the Code, or as a part of the cooking process. Pf Observed raw ROP chicken tenders thawing in Cambro submerged in running water at prep sink. Water was 80F. CDI: PIC instructed employee to move product to WIC to continue thawing on a speed rack. EHS discussed proper thawing parameters with PIC.

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. 
Observed stack of metal dishes on rack above 3 comp sink still sticky to touch.
CDI- Dishes re-w/r/s.

Observed tongs and spoons at cook line with oil and food debris from yesterday left at flat top overnight. EHS advises PIC on proper frequency of cleaning in-use utensils.
CDI- All cook line utensils w/r/s. (-1.5)

REPEAT.
3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed RTE chicken, egg rolls, and cooked veggies without date mark. EHS provided education to PIC and head chef about what items require a date mark and confirmed prep date of items.
CDI- Education provided, items date marked. (-3)

Reminder- the following need date marks if prepped and kept onsite more than 24 hours:
1. All cooked meats 
2. Cooked eggs and egg rolls 
3. Cooked plant food- rice, vegetables
4. Opened containers of milk 
5. Opened containers of soft cheeses 
6. Shrimp and hoisin sauce 
7. Slices lettuce, cabbage, and tomatoes 
8. Fresh garlic and oil mixtures 
9. Cooked noodles, lo mein 
Note: this list is not all inclusive, and is only a starting guide for relevant foods onsite.

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed cut salmon and cut chicken actively cooling in grill make unit. PIC stated salmon was placed into unit and cut an hour prior to inspection. after thirty minutes, EHS observed inadequate cooling rate (see temp chart). EHS observed cooked chicken bagged into sets for harissa chicken. EHS observed chicken above 41F (see temp chart). PIC stated chicken was placed into unit at noon but was left out unintentionally for longer than needed prior to being placed into unit so item needed to cool after. No temperature was checked after being placed into unit. EHS observed diced tomatoes being stored in WIC in numerous pans tightly covered with lid. PIC stated items should not be covered, and removed lid. EHS observed inadequate cooling rate after 25 minutes (see temp chart). PIC stated tomatoes were cut at 1:30pm. CDI - Due to having 15 minutes left to cool, PIC removed harissa chicken and placed into blast chiller to quickly cool. PIC removed salmon from make unit and placed into blast chiller. EHS observed chicken at 41 within 15 minutes. EHS observed salmon at 41F prior to end of inspection. PIC moved diced tomatoes to blast chiller. EHS observed adequate cooling rate by end of inspection. EHS advised to ensure temperatures are taken by staff throughout the day to ensure when items are moved they are cooled prior to storage, and to ensure proper cooling methods are followed. REPEAT. (1)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

violations.comments:
3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P EHS observed raw calamari stored over RTE foods in make unit reach in compartment. CDI - PIC rearranged storage order, no contamination observed. 
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. EHS observed raw calamari and raw turkey being prepped/thawed at three compartment sink with no visible separation or protection. PIC stated raw ground turkey was left at three compartment sink drain board to drain excess liquid. EHS observed raw calamari in the next compartment over thawing at room temperature. EHS advised to utilize prep sinks when preparing raw proteins and avoid using three compartment sink for these tasks. Facility has two prep sinks; one is a two compartment sink. CDI - PIC removed calamari and placed at empty prep sink under running water; ground turkey was moved to WIC. No contamination observed. 
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation(1.5)

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. EHS observed numerous pans and plastic containers stacked on top of each other, stored as clean, with visible sticker residue present on pans. CDI - PIC removed all pans with residue to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. (0)

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

3-501.14(B) Quickly cool TCS foods that are prepared from room temperature ingredients. Food must be to 41F within 4 hours. -P. EHS observed buffalo chicken dip in WIC at 44F. PIC stated dip was prepared yesterday and placed into WIC. PIC stated item has not left WIC since being placed there yesterday. EHS observed dip with tight fitting lid. EHS observed ground beef patties being cooled from preparation 3.5 hours prior to inspection. EHS observed patties at 45F with 15 minutes left to go, tightly covered with plastic wrap and lid. EHS intervened and advised PIC to move patties to freezer to quickly cool, so that the cooling parameter could be met. PIC stated temperatures have not been taken of these items during cooling process. EHS provided education. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded chicken dip, patties spread out and placed into WIF uncovered. EHS observed patties at 41, 15 minutes later. 
For more information, please visit: www.meckncgov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Cooling Food Safely https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6x8b1ZVOxU .


3-501.14(A) Quickly cool cooked foods within 2 hours from 135F to 70F; and within a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F. -P. EHS observed queso in WIC above 41F. PIC stated queso was made yesterday. Queso is split into smaller metal containers and left in WIC uncovered to cool. EHS observed film over queso, PIC stated item was not stirred frequently during cooling process. CDI - PIC voluntarily discarded queso.

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) EHS observed entire speed rack of prepared foods in WIC without proper dates. EHS advised that if numerous items are found without dates on next inspection, items could be required to be discarded. (0)

violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf EHS observed ground turkey, sweet potatoes, queso, and tomato sauce cooling at inadequate rates during inspection (see temp chart). EHS did not observe active monitoring of this process for any item during inspection. Tomato sauce observed in ice bath in prep sink, however, EHS observed no active stirring. 3-203.12 Retain tag on the bag of shellstock until empty. Record date on the tag when the last shellstock from the container is used. Store tags in chronological order for 90 days. -Pf

0 pts.

Observed one pan of roasted cauliflower date-marked with a prep date of 6/10, stored inside the lowboy portion of make table 1. Observed one pan of roasted cauliflower date-marked with a prep date of 6/11, stored inside the lowboy portion of make table 1. CDI: PIC voluntarily discarded potatoes, since it had surpassed the 7-day window.
Observed a pan of braised beef date-marked with a prep date of 6/10, stored inside the WIC. PIC stated this was the correct date of prep, but was frozen then thawed out 2 days prior.
CDI: PIC created second date label with thaw date of 6/16 to depict the "clock start date."
REPEAT VIOLATION.

violations.description: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
violations.comments:
3-501.19(B)(2) Follow written procedures for foods held using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for 4 hours. Ready to eat cut or chopped TCS produce or opened TCS hermetically sealed food that begins TPHC at 70 F or less, must remain at or below 70 F during the 4 hour time as a public health control period and be marked with the discard time. - Observed the egg wash container at the wok line to be held on TPHC but was not time stamped with a start or discard time. PIC stated it was brought out at approx 10:30am.

CDI - Cookline employee time stamped container.

3-501.13 (E ) Reduced oxygen packaged fish, required to be kept frozen until time of use per labeling, shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing under refrigeration or upon completion of thawing using running water. - Observed 3 vacuum sealed packages of raw tuna to be in the sushi counter lowboy refrigerator. Package thawing instructions stated “remove from packaging” and the packages observed at the time were fully intact.

CDI - Sushi employee moved to the WIC and placed on a sheet pan. Cuts were put into the packaging to remove them from the ROP environment.

violations.comments:
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P - Observed containers of grilled chicken strips, cut lettuce, and Swiss cheese to be in the cookline lowboy at temperatures of 44-49F. Items in the opentop are held using TPHC and were properly time stamped at the time of the inspection. PIC stated that staff leave the opentop open throughout lunch usually and stated that is why the lowboy is running warm. Ambient observed at 49F. PIC stated that the items have been in the lowboy since approx. 9am and were not sure how long the items have been out of temperature for. 

CDI - All out of temperature items voluntarily discarded. Ambient of the unit was observed at 41F and the lettuce moved up into the unit while the EHS was typing the report was able to hold/maintain 41F. EHS advised the staff to not keep the lid open during rushes or if they are going to do that they should not keep TCS foods in the lowboy portion as it causes temperature issues during that period.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

violations.description: Compliance with variance, specialized process, reduced oxygen packaging criteria or HACCP plan
violations.comments:
3-502.11 Obtain a variance for specialized processes.-Pf 
Observed facility is using a sous-vide method for braised lamb (which launched on new menu 6 weeks prior). PIC showed SOPs of the process, to which EHS found gaps in the process and observed SOPs were not a true HACCP plan. PIC stated that the lamb is received raw, cooked on the premises, cut into chunks, then mixed with a sauce, before they use a vacuum-sealer to vacuum-seal the marinated lamb chunks into packages, which are then held for a shelf-life of up to 2 days, which will be placed into the sous-vide per order. Upon communication with the Head Chef via phone, it was brought to EHS's attention that the corporate office has contacted the state for a variance letter, but facility has yet to receive the approval letter. EHS explained this method requires a variance from the state prior to executing this specialized process, and PICs understood.
CDI: All 4-oz ROP'd packages of braise lamb were voluntarily discarded by the PICs and menu item was 86'd for all dine-in and carry-out options. 
**NOTE: Per permit conditions...
- The PERMIT HOLDER shall not add equipment or change the menu prior to obtaining approval from the REGULATORY AUTHORITY. A
change in the type of food establishment or food operations is required to be approved by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY to ensure
compliance with the rules.
- Plans and specifications must be submitted for review and approval before any equipment is added or removed and /or remodeling of any
part of the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT premises.
- The PERMIT HOLDER shall obtain written approval from the REGULATORY AUTHORITY prior to beginning specialized methods of food
processing.
EHS provided PICs with resources for HACCP and Variance for specialized processes.

For more information on how to apply for a variance please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

violations.description: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. Cold air must flow around product to remove the heat. -Pf 
Observed pan of black pepper bean sprouts cooling inside the WIC and not changing in temperature after 38 minutes had surpassed. Pan was made of plastic and covered with a lid.
CDI: PIC moved pan into the standing reach-in freezer to rapidly cool down.
Observed several sheet trays full of cooked white rice cooling inside the WIC and not changing in temperature after 38 minutes had surpassed. Rice was not spread out evenly on sheet trays, and left in large chunks/piles. 
CDI: PIC had food employees break up the rice into small pieces and into the reach-in freezer to rapidly cool down. 
Observed pan of blanched thin rice noodles that had surpassed the cooling parameters and holding above 41F. Pan was made of plastic and lid was covered, and portioned bags inside the pan were filled past the fill line.
CDI: PIC voluntarily discarded rice noodles.
REPEAT VIOLATION.

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Cooling Food Safely https://youtu.be/P6x8b1ZVOxU .

REPEAT VIOLATION.

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P - Observed a container of tater tots to be at a temperature of 96F on the counter beneath the heatlamp at the cookline. PIC stated that they make the tater tots in the oven every day and then they sit under the heatlamp until needed. EHS advised the PIC that switching to TPHC could be more beneficial since they are often only open from 7-11pm and typically sell through it on busier weekend nights.

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) - Observed 2 opened packages of hot dogs in the lowboy refrigerator that were not provided with date marks of any kind. Upon questioning it was discovered they were opened the previous Wednesday, making today day 8 for the items. violations.comments:
3-501.15 Quickly cool foods. Use methods such as open/vented shallow pans, large ice baths and active stirring. violations.description: Food in good condition, safe & unadulterated
violations.comments: 3-101.11 Food shall be safe for consumption, unadulterated and honestly presented. -P -Observed tomato stored in prep unit with visible blue/white growth. -CDI- PIC voluntarily discarded the tomato.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P -Observed raw chicken and raw lamb stored above shrimp and cooked crab meat in the tall reach-in cooler. -CDI- Storage order was corrected.



For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P -Observed cooked mushrooms, raw shrimp, and cooked crab meat above 41F in tall reach-in cooler. All other TCS food in tall RIC was at or below 41F. PIC stated the mushrooms, shrimp, and crab meat were originally stored in the under-grill cold drawers this morning, yet the cold drawers have not been cold holding properly recently, so the food was moved to the tall RIC after realizing the cooler was malfunctioning again. PIC stated the cold drawers underneath flat top grill have not been cold holding below 41F recently, and they are waiting on cooler parts for repair. -Do not store TCS foods in the under-grill drawers until the cooler is fully repaired and properly maintaining food at or below 41F. -PIC stated the food was moved to the tall RIC less than one hour ago, therefore PIC placed mushrooms, crab meat, and shrimp on ice in tall RIC for rapid cooling. By end of inspection, EHS observed shrimp, mushrooms, and crab meat cooling at sufficient rates to reach 41F. -Contact EHS when cooler is repaired- 3 day verification visit required-
REPEAT

VERIFICATION REQUIRED to ensure menu is updated with disclosure.

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed duct tape wrapped around leg of dump sink to secure piping underneath. Removed duct tape and secure piping with a material that is smooth and easily cleanable.

5-202.14 Prevent backflow or back siphonage prevention devices installed shall meet American Society of Sanitary Engineering standards. -P Observed a hose leading from fixture at mop sink to sanitizer in 3 compartment sink in which no back flow device was on faucet fixture. CDI: PIC removed hose. No equipment or utensils were being sanitized.

violations.comments:
2-301.14 (E) Wash hands after handling soiled equipment or utensils. -P
Observed food employee drop thermometer on kitchen floor, Employee picked up thermometer and returned to food prep.
CDI - EHS intervened and Employee washed hands and donned new gloves.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P 
Observed portioned RTE beef balls stored in same container as portioned raw beef inside the prep unit. 
CDI - Beef balls removed 
Observed raw beef stored above crab Rangoon in prep unit.
CDI - Storage order rearranged. 


For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

4-602.11 (E )Clean the equipment and utensils used with nonTCS foods as required to avoid contamination.
Observed pink build-up on the interior of the ice machine.

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed multiple items previously prepared, frozen, removed from the freezer and no date mark/label was added (Beef Broth, brown rice, & Lo Mein). The date of prep and the thaw date should follow all items prepared and thawed at a later date for service.
CDI - The proper date marks were added to each food.



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

Observed TCS food items stored inside WIC 1 cold holding above 41F. Ambient air temp of WIC 1 was at 48F, and EHS noticed WIC door was left open, with employees constantly going in and out of the unit. Facility conducts equipment temperature checks and records temperatures digitally using tablets, but WIC 1 temperatures were not taken this morning. Ambient air temp dropped to 45F after 22 minutes. Another ambient air temp was taken at 11:30AM (over an hour from the first initial ambient air temp reading) after unit was blocked off from employee use, and WIC 1 was still temping 44F-47F (immediate spike in temperature when door is opened). EHS noticed ice buildup on fan inside the unit, and heavy condensation dripping from the fan. PIC entered a work order in for technicians to come out and check on the unit. All TCS food items from WIC 1 were moved into WIC 2, as WIC 2 has plenty of storage space to hold TCS food items. PICs stated they understand to keep raw chicken stored separated from all other TCS food items inside WIC 2. 
VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 3 days to ensure facility is in compliance.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

2-103.11(A-P) PIC shall ensure rules in the code for food safety and handling are met. -Pf Observed overall limited control over the kitchen by certified food protection manager. Ensure that staff are aware of cross contamination issues, allergens within products, and are monitoring temperatures. 




A Food Safety Checklist can be found at: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety along with more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.

3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P- Observed raw bacon stored over RTE sausage in RIC. -CDI- PIC corrected storage order. REPEAT VIOLATION
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(1) Maintain TCS foods in hot holding at 135F or above. -P Observed veggie omelet and turkey sausage held on counter with no temperature control below 135F. CDI: Omelets rapidly reheated to 169F. Sausage voluntarily discarded. 



For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P- Observed items in glass front reach in above 41F. -CDI- Refrigerator turned down. Items were placed in refrigerator at beginning of the morning and monitored while cooler recovered. PIC voluntarily discarded eggs. After 45 min, items holding at 41F. Future cold holding violations will result in a risk control plan and/or permit action. 

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 

Observed no date mark on hard boiled eggs or RTE sausage patties in reach in cooler. CDI: Items date marked with the date opened. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .
4-204.112 (B) Provide and position correctly an air thermometer in cold/hot holding equipment. Observed no air thermometer in glass reach in cooler.

3-602.11 (B) (5) Food packaged on premises for customer self service shall include a label with the major food allergens contained in the food -Pf. Observed individually wrapped muffins with no allergen labeling. VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 10 days to ensure that facility has allergens listed. 
3-602.11(C) Bulk food available for consumer self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled in plain view with the manufacturer label provided with the food, or another method of identification that includes the information in 3-602.11 (B)(1), (2), and (6). Observed bulk dispense cereals where common name of the food was incorrect (Raisin Bran identified as Special K Red Berries) and the other required information was missing. CDI: Information provided as required.

violations.description: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display
violations.comments:
3-306.11 Protect food on display using shields, packaging, or other effective means. -P Observed hard boiled eggs stored in an open container for customer self service inside of reach in refrigerator. CDI: Eggs voluntarily discarded. Eggs shall not be stored in this manner without a cover. 
3-306.13(B)(C) Consumer self-service operations shall have utensils or effective dispensing methods to protect the food from contamination and be monitored by trained food employees.-Pf Observed oatmeal toppings without proper protection or self closing lids. Ensure that staff are adequately monitoring toppings and/or proper protection is provided. VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 10 days to assess food protection. 
3-305.11 Store food in a clean, dry location, not exposed to contamination. Keep at least 6 inches above the floor. Observed employee’s hot tea stored on top of boxes of pancake mix. CDI: Tea relocated to designated area.

6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. Observed floor in dry storage area in need of sweeping. Observed dust build up on ceiling tiles adjacent to AC vent. 
6-101.11/6-201.11 Floors, walls and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable. Floors shall be non-absorbent in areas subject to moisture. Observed 1 absorbent ceiling tile in kitchen.

3-302.11 (A)(2) Separate types of raw animal foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display. -P. 
Observed a pan of marinated raw chicken skewers stored on a shelf above a pan of marinated raw red snapper, stored inside RIC 3.
CDI: PIC corrected storage order and EHS provided food storage order handout to serve as a visual aid.

For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation

3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed multiple TCS food items stored inside the lowboy cooler above 41F (see temp chart). Ambient air temp of the cold holding unit was 45F. PIC stated food items are not kept inside this unit overnight, and are pulled from the WIC in the morning. Food items have been stored inside this unit less than 4 hours. PIC moved all TCS food items into the RIF to rapidly cool down. PIC contacted technician to have cold holding unit checked for repairs. EHS checked ambient air temp again after PIC had manually adjusted temperature dial on the unit, and ambient air temp of the unit was now temping at 47F.
VERIFICATION REQUIRED within 3 days to ensure facility is in compliance.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Safe Food Temperatures https://youtu.be/tXP09IK-1TQ .

3-501.17 (A) or (B) Date mark/label all TCS foods that are ready-to-eat once opened or prepared and are to be held for more than 24 hours. -Pf. Establish a date marking system consistent with 3-501.17 (A) or (B). Additional date marking system options are found in 3-501.17 (D). 
Observed pan of paneer without a date label, stored inside the make table. PIC stated this was prepared yesterday.
CDI: Date label created.
Observed bottle of salad dressing (house-made w/TCS ingredients) without a date label, stored inside the lowboy cooler. PIC stated this was prepared on Sunday.
CDI: Date label created.
Observed pan of boiled potatoes and a pan of cut cabbage both missing date labels, stored inside the lowboy cooler. PIC stated these were prepared on Sunday as well.
CDI: Date label created. 
Observed opened jug of whole milk missing date label. PIC stated they opened this jug of milk on Sunday.
CDI: Date label created.
REPEAT VIOLATION.
*Note: Although a repeat violation, EHS not deducting full points today as facility has now established a date-marking system since previous inspection, and it appears some TCS food items were missed. PICs understood which food items require date labels and which do not, and understand that food items are not held past 7 days from prep.

For more information, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q0iLZb7v0UM and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

3-501.13 (E ) Reduced oxygen packaged fish, required to be kept frozen until time of use per labeling, shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing under refrigeration or upon completion of thawing using running water.
Observed ROP'd packages of raw salmon fillets thawing under running water, temping above 32F (no longer in the frozen state), without slits in the packaging.

violations.comments: 3-203.12 Retain tag on the bag of shellstock until empty. Record date on the tag when the last shellstock from the container is used. rows.general_comments:
Return visit to be made Monday, 06/01, to initiate a Risk Control Plan for multi-repeat priority violations. 
PIC and staff encouraged to reach out with any questions or support needs. Training visits and follow up compliance visits will be made as needed to support correction of non-compliant items. 

Inspection co-led by EHS Nicholas Suhocki.

violations.comments:
6-301.11 Provide soap for handwashing at each handsink. -Pf
Observed no soap at cook line hand sink.
CDI- PIC refills dispenser. (-0)

violations.description: Food in good condition, safe & unadulterated
violations.comments:
3-202.15 Food packaging must be in good condition, intact and protect the food inside. Pf
Observed leaking fan in WIC dropping large amount of water onto food below. Entry of water observed in multiple containers, as well as wet cardboard boxes and more than an inch of standing water on lidded/packed items.
CDI- items in sealed packaged verified without entry of water and removed to separate area. Contains with entry or water and food inside soaked cardboard boxes voluntarily disposed. A large metal container was placed to catch water. PIC should place work order for WIC. (-1)

REPEAT.
4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf. 
Observed numerous containers and utensils stored as clean on rack with visible food debris, grease, soap, and/or date mark sticker still remaining.
CDI- All dishes re-w/r/s. EHS advised PIC and dishwashing staff member about ware-washing efficacy. (-3)


4-501.114 Maintain sanitizer at correct concentrations when being used to sanitize. -P 
Observed quat above 450ppm in 3 comp sink at bar where sanitization of dishes occurs. 
CDI- Quat dilluted to 350ppm.

REPEAT.
3-501.16(A)(2) Maintain TCS foods in cold holding at 41F or less. -P 
Observed TCS dressings in ice bath at expo lowboy between 48-52F and portioned crab dip in cook line cold drawer between 44F-46F.
CDI- PIC voluntarily discards crab dip + dressings and restarts with new products below 41F on TPHC. EHS advises no TCS foods should be stored inside the expo lowboy without proper TPHC until it is repaired, with an ambient temp low enough to support maintaining TCS foods at 41F and below. Cold drawer across cookline should also be used with TPHC only until building AC is repaired and ambient temp in unit can support proper cold holding. (-3)

**EHS notes this is the fifth consecutive inspection with cold holding out of compliance. A return visit will be made Monday, 06/01, to initiate a Risk Control Plan in collaboration with PIC**

REPEAT.
3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) 
Observed portioned crab dip in cook line cold drawer expired yesterday. Points not escalated due to overall improvement to date marking onsite. (-1.5)

3-304.14(B) Hold in-use wiping cloths in properly concentrated sanitizer between uses.
Observed wiping cloths in 50PPM of quat. 
CDI- Sani-bucket sanitizer refilled to proper concentration. (-0)

REPEAT.
3-304.12 (D) When running water is used for storing utensils for moist foods, the water velocity must be sufficient to flush particulates to the drain.
Observed in use utensils covered in food debris in dipping well with inadequate water pressure to remove debris.
CDI- Water pressure increased, utensils brought to ware-washing for w/r/s. (-1)

2-301.12 (A),(B), (C) Wash hands for at least 20 seconds. Follow the cleaning procedure to adequately wash your hands. Use warm water, soap, scrub 10 to 15 seconds, rinse, and immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough hand drying method (ex. Disposable Paper Towel) and use a clean barrier such as a disposable paper towel when touching surfaces such as a manually operated faucet handle to avoid recontaminating hands. -P- Observed food employee wash hands and not use a barrier to turn off the faucet. -CDI- EHS educated food employee on using a barrier to turn off faucet and food employee rewashed hands.

2-301.14 (F) Wash hands during food preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination, and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks. -P- Observed food employee handling raw carne asada and then go to handle spice containers, date marking stickers, and pen without washing hands. Observed food employee handle raw fish and then go to handle water handle on coffee machine without washing hands. -CDI- EHS educated food employee on when to wash and food employee washed hands. -0-

violations.description: PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties
violations.comments:
2-102.11 (A) - (C )(1), (4)-(16) The Person in charge shall demonstrate knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of HACCP principles, and the requirements of this code by (A) Complying with the Food Code by having no violations of Priority Items during the current inspection, (B) Being a certified food protection manager, or (C) by responding correctly to the inspector's questions related to the operation of the food establishment. -Pf- Observed facilities lack of control of food safety measures in the facility and an inability to demonstrate knowledge on food safety principles. During inspection facility received 4 Risk factor violations. EHS spoke with PIC pertaining to food safety principles specifically referencing the risk factor violations from today’s inspection.
EHS will return to further evaluate facilities ability to demonstrate knowledge.





Please visit our resource page, www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety, for more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.

2-102.12 (A) PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by being a certified food protection manager. Observed no certified food protection manager present at the facility at the time of the inspection. Ensure that there is a CFPM present at the facility at all hours of operation. 






For more information on becoming a certified food protection manager please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

2-301.12 (A),(B) Wash hands for at least 20 seconds. Follow the cleaning procedure to adequately wash your hands. Use warm water, soap, scrub 10 to 15 seconds, rinse, and immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough hand drying method (ex. Disposable Paper Towel). -P- Observed food employee not use soap to wash her hands and only wash hands for approximately 5-10 seconds. Observed 2 other foods employees wash hands with soap but do so for approximately 5-10 seconds. -CDI- PIC Simon and EHS discussed proper hand washing procedures, hands were rewashed following proper procedures. 

For more information on handwashing, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link, https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M .

-Repeated failure to meet compliance with handwashing in the facility may lead to the facility being placed on a risk control plan for Handwashing-

4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf- Observed plastic cups used to make boba with a buildup of pink residue and debris present on them. Plastic cups were moved to the 3-Compartment sink and were washed/rinsed/sanitized using QUAT sanitizer. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean and maintained as clean. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

4-602.11 (E )Clean the equipment and utensils used with nonTCS foods as required to avoid contamination. Observed buildup of debris and residue present on the metal tray on the internal portion of the ice machine. Ensure that the ice machine is cleaned at a frequency to prevent buildup.

3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) Observed milk, whipping cream, and liquid yogurt in the lowboy cooler with no date marking present. PIC stated that they were working when all containers were prepped or opened. PIC backdated the containers with proper date marking. Ensure all TCS foods are date marked upon opening/prep. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

During inspection facility received 4 Risk factor violations. EHS spoke with PIC pertaining to food safety principles specifically referencing the risk factor violations from today’s inspection.
EHS will return to further evaluate facilities ability to demonstrate knowledge.





Please visit our resource page, www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety, for more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.

2 - Certified Food Protection Manager: 2-102.12 (A) PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by being a certified food protection manager. Observed no certified food protection manager present at the facility at the time of the inspection. Ensure that there is a CFPM present at the facility at all hours of operation. 






For more information on becoming a certified food protection manager please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

8 - Hands clean & properly washed: 2-301.12 (A),(B) Wash hands for at least 20 seconds. Follow the cleaning procedure to adequately wash your hands. Use warm water, soap, scrub 10 to 15 seconds, rinse, and immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough hand drying method (ex. Disposable Paper Towel). -P- Observed food employee not use soap to wash her hands and only wash hands for approximately 5-10 seconds. Observed 2 other foods employees wash hands with soap but do so for approximately 5-10 seconds. -CDI- PIC Simon and EHS discussed proper hand washing procedures, hands were rewashed following proper procedures. 

For more information on handwashing, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link, https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M .

-Repeated failure to meet compliance with handwashing in the facility may lead to the facility being placed on a risk control plan for Handwashing-

16 - Food-contact surfaces: cleaned & sanitized: 4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf- Observed plastic cups used to make boba with a buildup of pink residue and debris present on them. Plastic cups were moved to the 3-Compartment sink and were washed/rinsed/sanitized using QUAT sanitizer. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean and maintained as clean. 

For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: Sanitizing Solutions - https://youtu.be/ykP2mr9CtRg , How to Test Sanitizer https://youtu.be/y0SjmnabFaY , and Cleaning and Sanitizing Food Contact Surfaces https://youtu.be/av1Rbh-lh08 .

4-602.11 (E )Clean the equipment and utensils used with nonTCS foods as required to avoid contamination. Observed buildup of debris and residue present on the metal tray on the internal portion of the ice machine. Ensure that the ice machine is cleaned at a frequency to prevent buildup.

23 - Proper date marking & disposition: 3-501.18 Discard the food requiring date labels once time/temperature window has expired, if it has not been labeled, or if the label is incorrect. -P The PIC should train and assign staff to monitor date marking to prevent the use of food products that are no longer in compliance with 3-501.17 (A), (B), or (C) Observed milk, whipping cream, and liquid yogurt in the lowboy cooler with no date marking present. PIC stated that they were working when all containers were prepped or opened. PIC backdated the containers with proper date marking. Ensure all TCS foods are date marked upon opening/prep. 



For more information, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training videos at the following weblinks: What are TCS Foods https://youtu.be/bRvqAETDjQU and Date Marking Food Safely https://youtu.be/BOPsSNUajYs .

38 - Insects & rodents not present; no unauthorized animals: 6-501.111 Keep the premises free of insects, rodents, and other pests. Observed 2 small pests in the facility, 1 was present on the floor the other on the wall. Ensure that the premises is maintained free of pests. (Insect). PIC stated that the facility does routine pest control.

39 - Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage & display: 3-305.11 Store food in a clean, dry location, not exposed to contamination. Keep at least 6 inches above the floor. Observed several containers of dry flavors/powders for the teas stored on the counter uncovered with no lids. Ensure that all food is stored in a way so that it is not exposed to potential contamination.

40 - Personal cleanliness: 2-402.11 Use head coverings, beard guards and clothing to restrain body hair from contacting exposed food, equipment, and utensils. Observed 2 employees handling food without a head covering on. Ensure all food employees are wearing hair restraints/head coverings.

43 - In-use utensils: properly stored: 3-304.12 (F) Containers of water used for storing in-use utensils must be maintained at a temperature of at least 135 F and cleaned at least every 24 hours or when container has accumulated soil or residue. Observed a scoop in the jelly prep top that was stored in a container of water. The container of water was being maintained as cold.

49 - Non-food contact surfaces clean: 4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed bottom of blenders in the facility with a build up of residue and soil present and sticker residue present on the external surfaces of several containers being stored as clean. Observed low cabinets along the back wall of the drink prep area with debris and soiling present on the inside.

51 - Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices: 5-205.15 Maintain a plumbing system in good repair. Observed a drip underneath the PVC piping at the 3-Compartment sink. Ensure that the plumbing system is maintained in good repair and the leak is repaired.

55 - Physical facilities installed, maintained & clean: 6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. Observed walls of the facility with presence of soiling, observed soiled floors and buildup on floors specifically underneath the 3 compartment sink. Ensure that floors and walls are cleaned and maintained as clean.

rows.general_comments:
EHS observed prep unit with nonTCS sauces and heavy whipping cream above 41F. When EHS asked PIC about heavy whipping cream, PIC stated that it belonged to one of the other food employees. Prep unit must be repaired and only to be used to stored nonTCS items until repairs can be made. 

EHS observed multiple boxes of chicken sitting out at ambient air for extended amounts of time. When EHS asked PIC about chicken, PIC stated that it had just been delivered and that food employees were going to prep it. EHS observed temperature at 40-41F but educated PIC on ensuring that it is not left out of temperature control for extended amounts of time. PIC placed items in WIC.

Multiple cold holding units not properly functioning. Majority of items in WIC, reading at or above 41F. Items that were lower than 41F were stored in ice (i.e. raw chicken). PIC called repair person while EHS was present. Must receive confirmation/verification that cold holding has been repaired within the next few hours. 

When EHS arrived, carbon monoxide detector was alerting that levels were unsafe. EHS observed back hood not turned on. PIC turned on back hood and opened doors to allow for proper ventilation and carbon monoxide monitor showed safe levels. 

While EHS was typing, owner came in and wanted to carefully review all violations. Education provided and EHS placed emphasis on focusing on getting risk factor violations corrected and re-education/retraining staff. 

Observed no proof of MFU, Nohemy (31618). Observed no labeled or empty shelving in WIC or dry storage. PIC stated that MFU comes sometimes but not able to provide any additional information. Once Owner arrived, she confirmed that MFU does come occasionally but is not always working. She also confirmed that MFU does have designated shelving in WIC, but it’s not labeled and some of the restaurant items are stored on that shelf. Owner also confirmed that MFU does not have any dry storage items that she leaves behind at facility. EHS educated PIC that as a commissary, 1 shelf must be maintained in WIC and dry storage. 

For re-inspection please call 980-314-1620.

violations.comments:

 4-101.17 (A) Wood and wood wicker may not be used as a food contact surface. Observed wooden spoons throughout.

rows.general_comments:
Facility must develop SOPs for large dishes that cannot fit into 3-comp sink and use of 3-comp sink as prep sink OR remove large dishes and ONLY use 3-comp sink for washing dishes. Ensure that SOPs for using 3-comp sink as prep sink include how sink will be cleaned, following proper W/R/S procedures before and after use as prep sink. 

RCP will be implemented for date marking. 

EHS observed large pot of barbacoa sitting on the ground. PIC stated that it had just been cooked and there was no room to place it anywhere else but it would be placed back on burners once the burners were free. EHS educated PIC on ensuring that items are not left out of temperature control for extended amounts of time. At time of observation, temperature was observed above 135F. 

EHS observed shredded cheese sitting out during lunch service. PIC stated that shredded cheese was used for birria tacos during lunch rush. EHS educated PIC on ensuring item is not left out of temperature control for extended amounts of time or using TPHC. At time of observation, cheese was observed at 41F. 

ITS being issued for improperly functioning buffet style steam table. Cannot use until repaired or replaced. PIC stated that they have told owner multiple times that it was not functioning and he hasn’t replaced it. EHS observed 2 of the wells turned on but not producing any heat. However, hot items were stored in these wells.

During inspection, EHS asked PIC about process of shrimp ceviche, PIC stated that no heat is applied, and it is cooked with lemon. At end of inspection, while going over report, PIC stated that some hot water is poured over shrimp prior to it being prepared as ceviche but it is not fully cooked. PIC not able to tell EHS FC temperature of shrimp when hot water is applied.

EHS recommended PIC use goo-gone or some other strong adhesive remover to remover stickers from containers and then properly wash them. EHS also recommended facility change to a date-marking sticker that is easier to remove/clean. 

EHS educated PIC on ensuring that facility is properly reheating items to above 165F by verifying with thin probe thermometer.

Sliding display cooler to only be used for nonTCS items such as desserts and drinks or must be replaced. 

For re-inspection call 980-314-1620.

violations.description: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried & handled
violations.comments:
4-903.11 (A) Store cleaned equipment, utensils, linens in a clean, dry location; where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor. Observed clean dishes stored on floor in dry storage area. Observed box of clean silverware stored on floor in room where tortilla machine is located. Observed clean dishes stored beneath steam table with food debris. Per PIC, items beneath steam table and in tortilla machine room are not in use. 
4-903.11 (B) After cleaning and sanitizing, clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying and covered or inverted. Observed standing water and wet stacking with dishes stored as clean. -0-
4-901.11(A) After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall not be used until air dried or adequately drained before contact with food. Observed food employee grab clean items out of sanitizer water to use without ensuring items were air dried or drained. -CDI- EHS educated and items placed to air dry.

violations.description: Single-use & single-service articles: properly stored & used
violations.comments: 4-903.11(A)(C) Store single-use and single-service articles in a clean, dry location; where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor./4-903.11(C ) Single Service and Single Use items shall be kept in the original protective package or stored using other means that protect the item until used. Observed single use plates with heavy food splash and items outside of original protective package. -0-

violations.description: Equipment, food & non-food contact surfaces approved, cleanable, properly designed, constructed & used
violations.comments:
4-101.19/4-202.16 Non FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent 
cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. Observed rusted shelving above 3-comp sink and below prep tables. -0-
4-402.11 Fixed equipment shall be spaced to allow access for cleaning around the equipment or sealed to adjoining equipment or walls. Observed 3-comp sink and handsinks in need of recaulking or resealing to wall. Recaulk or reseal. 
4-501.11 Maintain equipment in good repair. Observed missing panels at hood system and missing panel at bottom of RIC. Observed buffet-style steam table not properly functioning. Repair or Replace. **ITS BEING ISSUED FOR STEAM TABLE**
4-501.12 Resurface or replace cutting surfaces that can no longer be effectively cleaned and sanitized. Observed 1 cutting board in need of replacement due to deep cuts and no longer being smooth and easily cleanable. Resurface or replace. 
4-205.10 Ensure equipment other than toasters, mixers, microwaves, water heaters and hoods is ANSI certified or equivalent. Observed sliding display cooler that was not ANSI approved used to hold non TCS items. Items were found above 41F. Facility to no longer use cooler to hold non TCS items. 
4-101.17 (A) Wood and wood wicker may not be used as a food contact surface. Observed large wooden spoons. Per PIC, items not in use. Not approved for FCS. Remove.

violations.description: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained & used; test strips
violations.comments:
4-302.14 Provide a test kit that accurately measures sanitizer concentrations. -Pf- Observed no chlorine sanitizer test kit for 3-comp sink. **10 DAY VERIFICATION REQUIRED** 
4-301.12(B) Sink compartments shall be large enough to accommodate immersion of the largest equipment and utensils.-Pf- Observed large pots that could not be fully emerged into 3-comp sink. Remove or create SOPs. **10 DAY VERIFICATION REQUIRED**
4-501.19 During manual warewashing, maintain the wash solution at a minimum of 110F or as otherwise allowed by the detergent manufacturer label. -Pf- Observed wash water at 87F during manual warewashing. -CDI- EHS educated PIC on proper temperatures and water temperature corrected to 112F. 
4-301.12(A) Provide a three compartment sink for manually washing, rinsing and sanitizing of equipment and utensils. -Pf- Observed PIC using small bucket of wash water to wash dishes. -CDI- EHS educated PIC on filling 3-comp sink with water during manual warewashing and PIC filled wash compartment of 3-comp sink. 
4-501.16 (B) Warewashing sinks used to wash produce or thaw food shall be cleaned and sanitized before and after each use. Observed raw meat being cleaned in middle compartment of 3-comp sink while dirty dishes were in other 2 compartments. -CDI- EHS educated PIC on ensuring that sink is cleaned before and after use and PIC voluntarily discarded items. -0.5-

4-601.11(C ) Keep non food contact surfaces of equipment clean to avoid build up of dust, food residue or debris.4-602.13 Non food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned frequently to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Observed NFCS of thermometer with food debris, mixer, exterior surfaces of spice containers, and shelving throughout in need of cleaning. Increased and more thorough cleaning frequency recommended. -0-

violations.description: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
violations.comments:
5-501.110 Keep waste stored in receptacles so waste is inaccessible to insects and rodents. Observed waste stored outside of trash and recycling bins. 
5-501.113(B) Keep dumpster, outside waste containers covered with tight-fitting lids or doors. Observed opened door on trash and recycling bins. 
5-501.114 Drains in dumpsters and waste containers shall have drain plugs in place. Observed missing drain plugs on trash bins. -0-

6-501.12 Floors, walls, ceilings including the attachments such as soap, towel dispensers; light fixtures; and heat/ac vent covers shall be clean. Caution should be used to minimize food exposure. Observed walls in need of cleaning, especially where soda bibs are stored. Observed water buildup in floor drain below prep sink. Per PIC, it is due to grease in drain. Increased and more thorough cleaning frequency recommended. -0-
6-501.114 Remove any items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as equipment that is nonfunctional or no longer used and litter. Observed some plates stored below steam table and silverware stored in tortilla machine room and other items throughout that per PIC, are no longer in use. Remove any items no longer in use.

rows.violation_text:
1 - PIC Present, demonstrates knowledge, & performs duties: 2-102.11 (A) - (C )(1), (4)-(16) The Person in charge shall demonstrate knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of HACCP principles, and the requirements of this code by (A) Complying with the Food Code by having no violations of Priority Items during the current inspection, (B) Being a certified food protection manager, or (C) by responding correctly to the inspector's questions related to the operation of the food establishment. -Pf.- Observed multiple risk factor violations throughout inspection, and no CFPM present. **10 DAY VERIFICATION REQUIRED** -1-
Please visit our resource page, www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety, for more food safety information related to PIC Duties, Training, and managing food safety.

2 - Certified Food Protection Manager: 2-102.12 (A) PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by being a certified food protection manager. Observed no CFPM present during inspection. **REPEAT** -1-
For more information on becoming a certified food protection manager please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

3 - Management, food & conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities & reporting: 2-103.11(O) Ensure food employees are informed of their responsibility to report required symptoms, illnesses and exposure. -Pf- Observed PIC not able to provide any proof that new food employee had received training of EHP. Observed no signed attestation of EHP. -CDI- EHS educated all and all signed EHP at time of visit. -0-
For more information on employee health policy, please visit: www.mecknc.gov/foodsafety

6 - Proper eating, tasting, drinking or tobacco use: 2-401.11 (A) Employees shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and other items needing protection can not result. Observed PIC chewing gum throughout entire inspection. -CDI- EHS educated PIC on designated areas. -0-

8 - Hands clean & properly washed: 2-301.12 (A),(B) (C) Wash hands for at least 20 seconds. Follow the cleaning procedure to adequately wash your hands. Use warm water, soap, scrub 10 to 15 seconds, rinse, and immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough hand drying method (ex. Disposable Paper Towel) and use a clean barrier such as a disposable paper towel when touching surfaces such as a manually operated faucet handle to avoid recontaminating hands. Observed food employee wash hands for less than 20 seconds and not use a barrier to turn off the faucet, thus recontaminating hands. -CDI- EHS educated food employee on proper handwashing procedure and food employee properly rewashed hands. 
For more information on handwashing, please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation or view our training video at the following web link, https://youtu.be/BH6CLGrH10M .
2-301.14 (I) Wash hands after engaging in other activities that contaminate hands. -P- Observed food employee change trash bag and begin to return to food prep without washing hands. Observed PIC leave outside of back door and begin to return to food prep without washing hands. -CDI- EHS intervened, educated all on when to wash and food employees washed hands. 
2-301.14 (F) Wash hands during food preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination, and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks. -P- Observed food employee double glove to handle raw shrimp and then remove top glove and begin to return to handle cooking utensils without washing hands. -CDI- EHS intervened, educated food employee on no double gloving and when to wash and food employee removed gloves and washed hands. -2-

10 - Handwashing sinks supplied & accessible: 5-205.11 (A) A handwashing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use -Pf.- Observed large pot stored in front of handsink at BOH. -CDI- PIC relocated items. 
5-205.11 (B) A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing -Pf.- Observed grater stored in handsink. Observed PIC use handsink to fill up a pot of water. Observed ice in handsink. -CDI- EHS educated PIC on proper use of handsink and items were removed and handsinks cleaned out. -0-

14 - Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction: 3-402.11 and 3-402.12 Provide records from supplier to guarantee fish served raw or undercooked is free of live parasites. -Pf- Observed no parasite destruction letter for shrimp ceviche. **10 DAY VERIFICATION REQUIRED** -1-

15 - Food separated & protected: 3-302.11(A)(1) Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods and washed/unwashed fruits and vegetables. -P- Observed raw shrimp stored over RTE onions in RIC. Observed raw beef stored over RTE fries in RIC. Observed bag of fries stored in container with raw pork in WIC. Observed raw pork outside of original packaging in WIF stored over cooked lengua. -CDI- PIC corrected storage order. 
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation
3-302.11(A)(8) Separate unwashed produce from ready-to-eat foods. Observed crates of unwashed limes and peppers stored over RTE pupusas and chicken wings and crates of unwashed limes and green onions over fries, RTE onions, and cilantro in WIC. 
For more information on food storage order please visit: https://health.mecknc.gov/envhealth/food-and-facilities-sanitation
3-302.11 (A)(4) Except when the food is being cooled, store food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. Observed no protective cover on fries, ham, hot dogs, and mozzarella cheese in RIC. Observed no protective covers on chicken for tacos, and vegetables in WIC. **REPEAT** -3-

16 - Food-contact surfaces: cleaned & sanitized: 4-601.11(A) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. -Pf.- Observed food debris and sticker residue on multiple dishes stored as clean. Observed dishes beneath steam table with food debris. -CDI- PIC moved items to dishpit to be W/R/S. Per PIC, dishes beneath steam table are not in use.

4-602.11 (A) (5) Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned, and sanitized per 4-702.11/4-703.11, at any time during the when contamination may have occurred. -P.- Observed 3-comp sink being used to prepare raw meat and then PIC begin to return to use it for cleaning dishes. -CDI- EHS intervened, educated PIC on cleaning 3-comp sink after use and PIC properly cleaned sink.

4-703.11 After cleaning, equipment, food contact surfaces, and utensils shall be sanitized using an approved method.-P- Observed some items being placed in drying side of 3-comp sink, without being placed in sanitizer and other items not fully submerged in sanitizer water due to sanitizer compartment being full. -CDI- EHS educated PIC on proper sanitizing methods and items were fully submerged to ensure proper sanitization.
